findings.title: The repository is SHALLOW (not 'pruned'), and the validator never detects shallowness: write-once, back-dating and the D-035/D-037 commit tolerances silently depend on clone depth
findings.reproduction: (1) git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository prints true. .git/shallow lists e8361b8 ('DG0 round 12 ...'), whose parent dcb289c is simply not fetched (log 06). D-035 and D-037 (decisions.md rows D-035 and D-037) describe this as a history 'truncated'/'pruned' in an earlier session. The commits are outside a shallow boundary, and a full clone (CI uses fetch-depth: 0) may contain them. No file in tools/gates or tools/agents mentions 'shallow'. (2) Consequence for write-once: r21-shallow-writeonce.mjs (log 05). In clone A, commit M rewrites the write-once round-20/qa-verifier.findings.json (F-DG0-242 High -> Low) and findings.json to match, then commit N follows. checkWriteOnce(A) reports 2 errors ('M event', '2 different contents'). In B = git clone --depth 2 file://A, checkWriteOnce(B) reports 0 errors, and no output says the repository is shallow. The same applies today to every write-once file changed before e8361b8 in every local validation (prefreeze, the qa dry-run, the auditor's clone). (3) Consequence for D-037: in a complete clone, every ancestor of the present gate/round source_commit is present, so an ABSENT fix_revision is provably not in that candidate. The tolerance at rules.mjs:696-698 then accepts exactly the failing case. The unit test 'D-037 / F-DG0-242' even accepts fix_revision '0'x40 for a closure verified in the gate round. The census (log 04, P1) finds 3 closures (F-DG0-226/227/228) whose verifying round-13 source_commit is present while the fix is absent, which is possible only because of the shallow boundary.
findings.expected: The validator detects a shallow repository (git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository). It reports this, and either refuses or runs history checks only when a documented shallow boundary is explicitly allowed. Commit-absence tolerances apply only to commits beyond that boundary, or only when the verifying round's own source_commit is also unavailable, never to a closure in the gate round. D-035/D-037 are corrected to say 'outside the shallow boundary' and state what a full-history (CI) run is expected to show.
findings.actual: History-based integrity checks pass or fail depending on clone depth, without any warning. Tolerances meant for 'pruned' commits also accept fabricated SHAs in a complete clone.
findings.fix_summary: D-038: the repo was SHALLOW not pruned (unshallow restored pre-round-12 commits as real ancestors). validateGate now refuses a shallow repository; gate judged against complete history (CI fetch-depth 0). Backup branch deleted so the round-18 orphan 450c756 is uniformly absent.

verification.note: git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository prints false in the working repository and in a --no-local clone. The pruned-era commits are real ancestors of HEAD: all 22 round source_commits except the D-034-orphaned 450c756 are present and ancestors, and 421c922 is an ancestor. On a --depth=1 --no-local clone, validate.mjs --stage DG0 reports the D-038 shallow error (exit 1); on a complete clone it does not. A clone disguised by deleting .git/shallow still fails closed ('write-once: cannot inspect git history'). CI checks out with fetch-depth: 0, so the refusal does not break CI.

findings.title: The D-037 re-point of F-DG0-150/151 to 421c922 leaves a permanent gate error in any clone that carries the backup branch, while a single-branch clone (CI) passes: the gate verdict depends on which refs the clone has
findings.reproduction: F-DG0-150/151 were last verified by code-security in round 18. stages.json round 18 has source_commit 450c756, which exists only on the local, unpushed branch backup/pre-writeonce-repair-565ab3f and is not an ancestor of HEAD (log 12). D-037 re-pointed their fix_revision to 421c922, which is an ancestor of HEAD but NOT of 450c756 (cb76260, the original, is). Running qa's dry-run docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/tests/real-repo-gate-blockers.mjs on a --no-local clone of HEAD (log 10) therefore reports 2 errors that finishing round 21 cannot clear: 'finding F-DG0-150 (Low): fix 421c922233 is not in the verified round-18 candidate (450c756f67)' and the same for F-DG0-151. The harness buckets them as 'PRUNED', but both commits are present. In a --single-branch clone, 450c756 is absent (log 12), so rules.mjs:696 skips the check and the same gate passes. This contradicts D-037's claim that the dry-run is clean of permanent blockers.
findings.expected: A gate's validation result does not depend on which unrelated refs a clone happens to contain, and F-DG0-150/151's metadata is consistent with the round that verified them. For example, their reporter re-verifies them in a round whose candidate contains 421c922. Alternatively, the fix_revision stays cb76260 and the round-18 source commit is preserved on a pushed ref.
findings.actual: Locally, with the backup branch, validateGate fails permanently on F-DG0-150/151. In CI or a single-branch clone it passes. Fail-closed locally, so no false approval, but the gate cannot pass on this repository as it stands.
findings.fix_summary: D-038: F-DG0-150/151 re-verified in round 22 against the current candidate (fix 421c922, ancestor of HEAD) so their closure is clone-independent; backup branch deleted removes 450c756's conditional presence.

verification.note: No ref contains 450c756 any more (the backup/ branch is gone). It survives only as a reflog-held unreachable object in the working repository. The real-repo dry-run on a --no-local clone reports 0 in the PRUNED, RECORD-LESS and DROPPED buckets. Before this round's re-verification, a local clone that still holds 450c756 reports 2 extra errors for F-DG0-150/151 (dryrun-clone-modes.log). With the round-22 re-verification in place, both clone modes give 0 (f161-reverify-sim.log), so the verdict no longer depends on refs. This closure depends on the F-DG0-150/151 entries in this same sidecar being imported. The general object-store-vs-reachability issue is part of F-DG0-164.

findings.title: Residual 7 still frames the /proc/sys write as a file-tool path, but the agent's Bash shell can open DAC-writable host-global /proc/sys entries for write directly; the new comment's '(userns default)' names the wrong mechanism
findings.reproduction: Probes open(O_WRONLY) and close without writing, so no tunable was changed (logs 13 and 14). From the agent shell (uid 0, NoNewPrivs 1, in its own PID namespace), /proc/sys/vm/swappiness, kernel/shmmax, net/ipv4/ip_forward, vm/drop_caches and kernel/panic all open for write. docs/delivery/threat-model.md:60 (residual 7) describes the exposure as a file tool writing 'directly or by racing a symlink past the guard', and only withdraws the shell claim as 'unverified'. It is now verified that a plain shell redirect reaches these entries, with no race needed. The impact class is unchanged: host availability / kernel tunables, not repository or gate integrity. The /proc/sysrq-trigger vector does not exist on this kernel. Separately, tools/agents/agent_sandbox.py:153 says candidate code in the reviewer's fresh-procfs sandboxes sees /proc/sys read-only '(userns default)'. That holds for tools/gates/sandbox-run.sh only because of its explicit '--ro-bind /proc/sys /proc/sys' (log 13: EROFS). A plain nested 'bwrap --unshare-user --proc /proc' leaves /proc/sys writable.
findings.expected: Residual 7 states that the agent shell, as well as the file tools, can write uid-0 DAC-writable /proc/sys entries directly. The comment attributes the read-only /proc/sys in sandbox-run.sh to its explicit --ro-bind.
findings.actual: The residual understates the vector (shell, no race needed), though not the impact. The comment names the wrong mechanism. I would accept this as an observation: the disclosed impact scope (host-global availability, no integrity effect) is accurate, and F-DG0-149 already carries it.
findings.fix_summary: D-038: residual 7 now states the agent Bash shell (not only file tools) writes host-global /proc/sys directly (verified, no race); comment attributes read-only /proc/sys to sandbox-run.sh's explicit --ro-bind, not a userns default.

verification.note: Wording verified against behaviour. The agent shell opens /proc/sys/vm/swappiness, kernel/shmmax, net/ipv4/ip_forward, kernel/panic and vm/drop_caches for write (open(O_WRONLY)+close only; nothing written). Inside tools/gates/sandbox-run.sh the same entries are 'Read-only file system', because of its explicit '--ro-bind /proc/sys /proc/sys' (sandbox-run.sh:36). Residual 7's body and the agent_sandbox.py comment (lines 149-155) now state exactly this. Cosmetic nit: residual 7's bold heading still reads 'file-tool writes to uid-0-writable /proc/sys entries', while the body correctly covers the shell.

findings.title: Schema subset validator: additionalProperties:false does not reject keys named after Object.prototype members (constructor, toString, __proto__, hasOwnProperty)
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/schema.mjs:59 looks up props[key] on a plain object literal, so props['constructor'] resolves to Object.prototype.constructor, which is truthy. The value is then 'validated' against a keyword-less function and accepted, and the additionalProperties:false branch is never reached. With schema {properties:{a:string}, additionalProperties:false}, validate() reports 'zzz' as unexpected but accepts 'constructor', 'toString', '__proto__' and 'hasOwnProperty' (r21-schema-proto-keys.mjs, log 17). The gate rules read only named fields, so an extra key of this kind cannot change a verdict today.
findings.expected: Use Object.hasOwn(props, key) (and Object.hasOwn(value, key) for required), so every unexpected key is reported.
findings.actual: Prototype-named extra keys pass records, findings and gate schemas silently. I would accept this as an observation: no rule reads such keys.
findings.fix_summary: D-038: schema.mjs uses Object.hasOwn(props,key) and Object.hasOwn(value,key), so extra keys named after Object.prototype members (constructor/toString/__proto__/hasOwnProperty) are rejected by additionalProperties:false. Test D-038/F-DG0-163.

verification.note: schema.mjs uses Object.hasOwn for both required and properties. SEC22-7: additionalProperties:false now rejects constructor, toString, hasOwnProperty, valueOf, __proto__ (own key via JSON.parse), __defineGetter__ and isPrototypeOf, and a required 'constructor' is reported missing when absent. Unit test 'D-038 / F-DG0-163' passes.

findings.title: The D-037 absent-commit tolerance (commitPresent) is not scoped to genuinely pruned commits. checkInvocation now accepts a GATE-round review or audit run whose meta.head_commit_at_start is missing, null, the runner's own fallback 'unknown', or any non-existent 40-hex id. This reopens the round-9 QA5-N52/N53 controls (F-DG0-212 binding: the run must start from a commit that contains the frozen manifest). checkClosure likewise accepts a non-existent (typo'd or all-zero) fix_revision on a closure verified in a round whose own source_commit is present, including the gate round.
findings.reproduction: QA_REPO_ROOT=<fresh clone of a0e077d> node --test docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/tests/dg0-gate-negative-r21.test.mjs (log docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/round-21/11-qa21-negative-tests.log). On the independent fully-evidenced fixture (0 errors as control, QA21-G0), for each of domain-reviewer, code-security-reviewer, qa-verifier and release-auditor in the gate round, rewrite the run's meta.json: QA21-C4 head_commit_at_start = 'f'x40, QA21-C5 field deleted, QA21-C5b null, QA21-C5d 'unknown' (tools/agents/run-agent.sh:64 writes exactly this when `git rev-parse HEAD` fails). validateGate(current) returns 0 errors in all 16 cases (ACCEPTED). The round-9 suite re-run under round-21 rules (log round-21/10-r20-suite-rerun.log, QA20-G1) now fails QA5-N52 and QA5-N53, which passed through round 20. QA21-C3: a closure verified in the gate round (round-2, source_commit present) with fix_revision = the real fix with its last hex digit changed, or '0'x40, gives 0 errors. In a full clone a missing commit can never be an ancestor of a present one, so this is provably not 'in the candidate'. The existing unit test 'D-037 / F-DG0-242' (validator.test.mjs line ~1115) codifies the all-zero case in the gate round as accepted. Root cause: rules.mjs checkInvocation calls `if (commitPresent(repo, meta.head_commit_at_start)) {...}` and checkClosure calls `commitPresent(fix) && commitPresent(round.source_commit) && !isAncestor(...)`. Any value that does not resolve, whatever its shape and whichever round it is in, is treated as 'pruned'. Controls: a PRESENT fix that is not in the candidate is still rejected (QA21-C1 descendant, QA21-C2 dangling), and the real-repo dry-run is clean (round-21/13-real-repo-gate-blockers.log).
findings.expected: D-037 states that the tolerance covers commits 'pruned by a later legitimate history correction (the pre-round-12 truncation, the D-034 rewrite)', and that 'a run that started before the manifest is still caught'. By the same reasoning as D-036/F-DG0-240 (the D-035 tolerance must not reach the gate's own round), the tolerance should apply only to (a) a well-formed ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ value, never to a missing, null, 'unknown' or other malformed head_commit_at_start (those were rejected before D-037), and (b) a round that is itself pruned, i.e. whose source_commit is also absent, and never to the gate round. This is feasible on the real history: every one of the 33 record runs with an absent head_commit_at_start belongs to rounds 1-12, whose source_commits are all absent, and all 61 verifier runs with an absent head belong to pruned rounds. For closures, only F-DG0-226/227/228 (verified in round 13, present, fix d1352f4 absent) would need their fix_revision re-pointed at a retained commit that contains the fix, as was done for F-DG0-150/151. findings.title: agent_sandbox.py finish(): when one of the role's own new review files already exists in the real directory (another run of the same role and round committed it after this run's prepare), copy-back crashes with an uncaught FileExistsError. It leaves a partial copy-back (files sorted before the collision are already in the real tree) and writes no sandbox.json, contrary to the threat model's statement that discarded writes are listed in sandbox.json
findings.reproduction: Disposable fixture under $TMPDIR (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/round-17/12-copyback-collision-probe.log, script included). `agent_sandbox.py prepare qa-verifier ...`, then in the staging copy write round-2/qa-verifier.findings.json and round-2/qa-verifier.json. Then create round-2/qa-verifier.json in the REAL reviews dir (a concurrent run of the same role committing first). `agent_sandbox.py finish <state> <out>` exits 1 with 'FileExistsError: [Errno 17] File exists: .../round-2/qa-verifier.json' (the O_EXCL open). The real round-2 now holds THIS run's qa-verifier.findings.json next to the OTHER run's qa-verifier.json, and <out>/sandbox.json is not written. The real record is not overwritten (QA17-S4 passes on that point).
findings.expected: A collision on the role's own new file is handled like the other refusals: nothing is copied for that file, the collision is listed in sandbox.json 'discarded' (for example 'exists in the real tree (written concurrently); not copied'), finish() exits 3, and ideally no file of the run is copied back at all when any of them collides (check first, then copy), so the real tree never holds a mixed record/sidecar pair.
findings.actual: Fail-closed only. run-agent.sh treats any non-zero finish as SANDBOX_RC and a review run then exits 73 without auto-committing, the real record is preserved (O_EXCL), and a mixed pair would not bind to one run's transcript under D-021. It needs two concurrent runs of the same role for the same round, which the orchestrator does not schedule. But the evidence the threat model promises (sandbox.json with the discard list, meta.process_sandbox_*) is missing for that run, and an uncommitted foreign sidecar is left in the real reviews directory for the orchestrator to notice. Low and non-mandatory. I would accept it as an observation for DG0.

findings.title: D-038 scoping is keyed on a forgeable, object-store-based 'round absent' test: a superseded round whose frozen manifest records a non-existent source_commit re-opens the absent-fix tolerance, so a CLOSED_VERIFIED finding passes with an all-zero or typo'd fix_revision and the gate-candidate ancestry check is skipped
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:725-733 (checkClosure) sets roundAbsent = !commitPresent(round.source_commit), and when the fix_revision is also absent it pushes no error. The gate check at :731 sits only in the fix-PRESENT branch. round.source_commit is metadata: checkReviewRounds (:749) only requires it to equal the round's committed manifest.source_commit, and findManifest (:903-909) tolerates a manifest whose source_commit does not exist. Nothing requires a non-gate round's source_commit to exist or to be an ancestor of the commit that froze its manifest. Reproduction on the validator's own fixture (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-22/sec22-repro.tests.mjs.txt, run by run-sec22-repro.sh on a --no-local clone of 7cf94db; log sec22-repro.log): round 2 verifies F-DG0-101 (High, mandatory); round 3 is the gate round. The round-2 manifest is committed with source_commit 'deadbeef'x5, and real round-2 runs start from the commit that contains it. SEC22-1 (real fix): 0 errors. SEC22-2 (fix_revision = 0x40): 0 errors. SEC22-3 (fix_revision = one-character typo of the real fix): 0 errors. SEC22-4 control: a PRESENT off-branch fix is still caught ('is not in the gate candidate'). Retained and gate rounds hold (SEC22-5: unknown/HEAD/missing/null/zeros/uppercase/short heads and zero/f fix_revisions are all rejected). The same predicate gates checkInvocation's head tolerance (:399/:408), so in such a round a fabricated 40-hex head_commit_at_start is also accepted. Second symptom of the same root cause: commitPresent (:595-602) tests object-store membership, not reachability. The working repository still holds round 18's 450c756 through its reflog, while a --no-local clone does not, so validateGate(current) on the same commit differs by 2 errors (F-DG0-150/151 'fix 421c922 is not in the verified round-18 candidate') between the two clone modes (dryrun-clone-modes.mjs/.log). Why the tolerance has no remaining legitimate use: the validator now refuses shallow clones (F-DG0-160), and in a complete clone every ancestor of the gate source_commit is present. An absent fix_revision is therefore provably NOT in the gate candidate. Census on a --no-local clone (tolerance-census.log): 0 findings have an absent fix_revision; the only absent round is 18; and the only closures whose verifying run has an absent head are F-DG0-150/151, which this round re-verifies in round 22 (f161-reverify-sim.log: afterwards 0 dependent errors in both clone modes).
findings.expected: D-038 states the tolerance is 'never a retained round'. Retained-ness must not be something a single metadata value can declare. After this round nothing needs the absent-fix tolerance, so: (1) in checkClosure, reject any CLOSED_VERIFIED fix_revision that is not present AND an ancestor of the gate source_commit (and of the verifying round's source_commit when present), with no round-absent escape; (2) in checkInvocation, either drop the absent-head tolerance or restrict it to an explicit, reviewed allowlist of orphaned rounds (round 18, D-034); (3) decide 'absent' deterministically, e.g. by 'not an ancestor of HEAD' rather than by object-store membership, so unreachable reflog objects cannot change a verdict; (4) optionally, for a non-gate round whose manifest source_commit is present, require it to be an ancestor of the commit that introduced the manifest. Add fixture tests for SEC22-2/3.

findings.title: Findings sidecars in non-gate rounds are not bound to any run, and the latest raising sidecar supersedes the reviewer's immutable fields, so an added later-round sidecar can silently downgrade a finding's severity and mandatory_violation
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:495 keeps only the LATEST sidecar version of each finding ('later rounds supersede earlier versions'), and :537-539 compares findings.json's IMMUTABLE_FINDING_FIELDS (stage_id, requirement, severity, mandatory_violation, title, reported_by) against that version only. A <role>.findings.json is bound to a run's tool-authored outputs only for the gate-round records (checkReview :463). checkClosure binds only the verifications sidecar (:714), and checkReviewRounds (:752-763) only checks that a listed record's sidecar exists. write-once (:781) forbids modifying committed files, not adding new ones. Reproduction (sec22-repro.tests.mjs.txt SEC22-8, log sec22-repro.log): genuine 3-round fixture, with F-DG0-101 raised High/mandatory in round 1, verified in round 2, gate round 3; control 0 errors. With no reviewer run, add docs/delivery/reviews/DG0/round-2/code-security-reviewer.findings.json re-listing F-DG0-101 as Low / mandatory_violation false, and set the same values in findings.json: 0 errors. Negative control: the same findings.json downgrade WITHOUT the added sidecar is caught ('severity in findings.json ("Low") differs from the reviewer's ("High")').
findings.expected: A reviewer's classification of a finding can change only through a sidecar that the reviewer's own run demonstrably wrote. Either bind every findings sidecar (any round) to its role's run for that round, i.e. require it to be among that run's tool-authored outputs, as checkReview does for the gate round; or compare the immutable fields against EVERY raising sidecar version (or the earliest), so a later version cannot differ.
findings.actual: An added, unbound findings sidecar in any non-gate round later than the raising round re-classifies a High/mandatory finding as Low/non-mandatory without a validator error. Closing it still needs bound reviewer and auditor runs (for example ACCEPTED_OBSERVATION, which is only allowed for Low non-mandatory findings), so the effect is a misrepresented finding presented to those reviewers, not a direct gate pass. Hence Low.

findings.title: checkClosure still skips the 'fix is in the verified round candidate' check when the verifying round's source_commit is absent, a predicate that forged round metadata alone can satisfy. A PRESENT fix committed after the verifier's run started (so absent from both the round candidate and the run's head) still closes the finding
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:733 runs `if (commitPresent(repo, round.source_commit) && !isAncestor(fix, round.source_commit))`. round.source_commit is orchestrator metadata that checkReviewRounds (:752) only requires to equal the round manifest's source_commit, and findManifest (:895-913) tolerates a manifest whose source_commit does not exist. SEC23-7 in docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-23/sec23-repro.tests.mjs.txt (run by run-sec23-repro.sh on a --no-local clone of 6438e20; log sec23-repro.log) sets up round 2 to verify F-DG0-101 (High, mandatory) and round 3 as the gate round on a new candidate. The fix commit is a content change committed AFTER round 2's runs started, so it is not an ancestor of the round-2 verifier's head_commit_at_start (fix-in-verifier-head=false). Control, round 2 genuine (source_commit present): 1 error, 'fix … is not in the verified round-2 candidate'. Forged, round 2's committed manifest and stages entry name source_commit 'deadbeef'x5, entries self-consistent: 0 errors. D-039 closed the ABSENT-fix variant (SEC23-2/3: all-zero and typo'd fixes are rejected), and the fix must still be an ancestor of the gate candidate (SEC23-4). What remains is only the round-level binding: the reviewer's PASS is recorded as verifying a fix its run could not have seen. Real-repo census (tolerance-census.log): the only absent round is 18, and no CLOSED_VERIFIED closure is verified in round 18. So the skipped branch has no legitimate use today and is reachable only through forged round metadata. Exploitation still needs a genuine reviewer PASS verification in the forged round, so the effect is a mis-attributed fix_revision, not an unfixed finding in the gate candidate.
findings.expected: A CLOSED_VERIFIED closure must be tied to content the verifying run could actually see, whatever the round metadata says. Two options: (a) additionally require isAncestor(fix_revision, meta.head_commit_at_start) of the verifying run (always present and 40-hex after D-039, and a descendant of the round's source_commit in every legitimate case); or (b) reject a CLOSED_VERIFIED closure verified in a round whose source_commit is absent (no current closure depends on one). Optionally also require head_commit_at_start to be reachable from HEAD (isAncestor(head, HEAD)), not merely present in the object store, so an unreachable local object cannot change a verdict between clone modes (fail-closed in CI today). Add a fixture test like SEC23-7.

findings.title: D-040 replaced the round-candidate ancestry check instead of adding to it. In a GENUINE round (no forged metadata), a candidate-scope fix committed after the round froze but before the verifier's run started now closes a finding even though it is not in the frozen candidate the verifier reviewed. Round 23's validator rejected this
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:737-739 (at 6db3b83) now checks only isAncestor(fix_revision, verifyingRun.head_commit_at_start). The earlier `commitPresent(round.source_commit) && !isAncestor(fix, round.source_commit)` check was removed, not kept alongside. checkInvocation (:388-405) requires the head to be present, 40-hex and to contain the round manifest. Nothing requires the head's candidate CONTENT to equal the round candidate, i.e. that only metadata was committed between the freeze and the run start. SEC24-6 in docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-24/sec24-repro.tests.mjs.txt (run by run-sec24-repro.sh on --no-local clones; log sec24-repro.log) uses the stock fixture. Round 2 is genuine (its source_commit is present). A content change to src/app.txt is committed after the round-2 freeze, the round-2 runs start from that commit, the round-2 code-security run verifies F-DG0-101 (High, mandatory) with fix_revision = that commit, and round 3 is the gate round on a candidate containing it. Probe output: 'fix in round-2 frozen candidate: false; verifier head content hashes to round-2 candidate: false'. At 6438e20 (round-23 baseline): 1 error, 'fix … is not in the verified round-2 candidate'. At 6db3b83 (this candidate): 0 errors.
findings.expected: A CLOSED_VERIFIED closure stays bound to the frozen candidate the verifying round reviewed, as well as to the run head. Either (a) keep the D-040 run-head check AND restore `if (commitPresent(round.source_commit) && !isAncestor(fix, round.source_commit)) error`, or preferably (b) in checkInvocation, when binding.manifestPath is given, require candidateId(manifestFromRef(head, manifest.spec)) to equal the round's candidate_id. That means only metadata-only commits between the freeze and the run start. It binds the run head's content to the reviewed candidate and makes the run-head ancestry check equivalent to 'in the reviewed candidate'. The real-repo census (closure-census.log, --no-local clone) shows all 61 computable review-run heads already hash to their round candidate. The 2 non-computable runs are round 18's D-034-orphaned heads, and neither is a verifying or gate run. Option (b) therefore breaks no genuine record. Also correct the checkClosure error text 'it was not in the candidate the reviewer saw' (:739), which the head check does not establish without (b). Add a fixture test like SEC24-6.

So this is a mis-attribution, not an unreviewed fix in the gate. Real-repo census: 0 of 110 closures depend on it.

findings.title: D-044 claims every commit-id field the gate depends on must be a commit object, but a review round's source_commit (stages.json review_rounds[].source_commit and the round manifest) still accepts an annotated-tag object id
findings.reproduction: Candidate 331407e (sha256:1af91e8f...). D-044 (docs/delivery/decisions.md:39) says the change closes 'the whole "tag object id where a commit is required" class in one pass' and lists 'every commit-id field the gate depends on'. The gate source_commit (rules.mjs:966, D-037), fix_revision (rules.mjs:744) and head_commit_at_start (rules.mjs:399) are type-checked. A review round's source_commit is not: findManifest recomputes the round manifest with manifestFromRef(repo, m.source_commit, ...) (rules.mjs:918), which peels a tag to its tree; checkReviewRounds (rules.mjs:774-775) only compares the manifest's source_commit with stages.json; and checkClosure's anchor 1 uses commitPresent(round.source_commit) (cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}, which peels) and isAncestor (merge-base --is-ancestor, which peels) at rules.mjs:750-752. Probe SEC28-8 (test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-28/sec28b-roundsource.tests.mjs.txt, run in a disposable --no-local clone at 331407e): in the stock fixture, `git tag -a sec28round <frozen commit>` gives a tag object; a round manifest with source_commit set to that tag id makes findManifest return 0 errors, and `merge-base --is-ancestor <fix> <tag>` is true (peeled). Not reachable through the tooling: candidate.mjs --freeze writes `git rev-parse HEAD` (candidate.mjs:49/68/71), so only a hand-forged freeze could store a tag id. The gate ROUND can't hold one either, because its manifest source_commit must equal the commit-typed gate source_commit. The real repository is clean: all 27 resolvable round source_commits are commit objects; round 18 is the known D-034/D-035 absent one (objtype-census.log).
findings.expected: Consistent with D-044's stated scope: every commit-id field that a gate decision depends on, including review_rounds[].source_commit and the round manifest's source_commit, must be a commit object (objectType === 'commit'), with a tag rejected as for the gate source_commit. Otherwise D-044 should say that round source_commits are excluded, and why.
findings.actual: A tag-object round source_commit is accepted by findManifest, checkReviewRounds and checkClosure anchor 1: each peels it to the commit it names. This fails closed rather than open. The tag only aliases the same commit, so the content recompute and the ancestry anchors judge the correct commit. If the tag is deleted, a fresh clone lacks the tag object (SEC28-8: after tag -d + gc it's absent), and anchor 1 then rejects any closure verified in that round (F-DG0-169, SEC27-3). The residual is the same ref-dependent traceability-pointer inconsistency that F-DG0-250 fixed for fix_revision, plus the overstated completeness claim in D-044. It is not a gate bypass.

findings.title: Concurrent business-unit re-parenting commits a hierarchy cycle (A->C->B->A) through the API: the 'no cycles' rule is an unserialized API check with no database guard
findings.reproduction: apps/api/src/modules/organization/routes.ts:335 locks only the MOVED unit (findBusinessUnit(tx, id, true)); :348 checks isDescendant() (repository.ts:59, a read of the business_unit_closure view) under READ COMMITTED; :371-376 then UPDATEs parent_business_unit_id. packages/db/migrations/0001_identity_access.sql:68 states 'no cycles: API check' and there is no trigger/constraint behind it (only business_unit_not_own_parent, a 1-cycle check). Inputs: BUs B (root), C (child of B), A (root) in one organization; an org-level business_unit.manage holder sends PATCH /api/v1/business-units/A {parentBusinessUnitId: C} and, concurrently, PATCH /api/v1/business-units/B {parentBusinessUnitId: A} (If-Match "1" each). The second request's FOR UPDATE row (B) is not locked by the first, so its cycle check reads the committed hierarchy (A is still a root) and passes; only its FK check then waits on A, AFTER the check. Deterministic reproduction through the real API on a disposable PostgreSQL 16 (test-only advisory-lock parking trigger, same technique as access-derived-race.test.ts): docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/code-security/round-1/repro-bu/zz-review-bu-hierarchy.test.ts (SEC-1), log repro-bu/repro-bu.log. The sequential control is correctly refused (422 business_unit.cycle). A 2-cycle (X->Y with Y->X) happens to be serialized by the FK's KEY SHARE lock on the new parent (repro-bu/repro-bu-attempt1-2cycle-serialized.log); a 3-cycle is not.
findings.expected: At most one of the two moves succeeds; the other is refused with 422 business_unit.cycle (or 409), and the committed hierarchy stays a forest. Fix options: serialize hierarchy moves per organization (e.g. SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the organization row or pg_advisory_xact_lock(org) before the cycle/depth checks), or enforce acyclicity in the database (constraint trigger on business_unit that walks the parent chain), plus a concurrency test.
findings.actual: Both PATCHes return 200 and the committed rows are parent(A)=C, parent(C)=B, parent(B)=A. business_unit_closure then yields 11 rows with A as descendant, truncated at depth 10. The three units are detached from any root, and downward-inheriting grants on any of them (e.g. TO/AUD at B) now apply to all three, including A's records, which were never under B. The depth limit (MAX_BU_DEPTH) races the same way.

history.note: raised by code-security-reviewer DG1 round 1; reproduced through the API on a disposable PostgreSQL 16 (proposed ID; the orchestrator may renumber)

findings.fix_summary: Migration 0009 adds a DB hierarchy-guard trigger + pg_advisory_xact_lock + locking ancestor walk + pre-check; the API takes the same lock before its cycle/depth checks. A cycle cannot commit even under concurrency. New integration test proves it; reviewer repro now fails.

verification.note: Fixed on candidate e6979e12 (source 485e91f). packages/db/migrations/0009_business_unit_hierarchy_guard.sql:38-92 adds an AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF parent_business_unit_id, organization_id row trigger. It takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(730219, hashtext(organization_id)) and walks the parent chain with SELECT ... FOR SHARE, raising 23514 business_unit_acyclic / business_unit_max_depth. apps/api/src/modules/organization/routes.ts:364 takes the same lock (repository.ts:80-84) BEFORE the FOR UPDATE read and the friendly checks, and :424 maps a trigger refusal to the existing 422 problems. A composite FK (0001:86-87) already rules out cross-organization parents, so a per-organization lock key is sufficient. Re-ran my round-1 repro UNCHANGED (repro-bu/round1-repro-rerun.log): SEC-1 no longer reaches its vulnerable outcome; it times out waiting for a row-lock waiter because the second PATCH now queues on the hierarchy advisory lock. My adversarial round-2 repro (repro-bu/zz-review-r2-bu.test.ts, 7/7 PASS in repro-r2-bu.log) results: (R2-1) the exact round-1 API interleaving gives A->C 200 and B->A 422 business_unit.cycle, with 0 cycles in business_unit_closure; (R2-2) the sequential friendly 422 still holds; (R2-3) direct SQL as mth_app at READ COMMITTED with no API lock gives the loser 23514 business_unit_acyclic; (R2-4) at REPEATABLE READ with the snapshot taken before the winner commits, the loser gets 40001 from the guard's FOR SHARE walk; (R2-5) one multi-row UPDATE putting two roots under each other gives 23514; (R2-6) mth_app cannot SET session_replication_role, ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER or replace the function (42501 x3). The attempt-1 log is kept: my harness waited only for advisory waiters, but at DB level the loser queues on the winner's FOR SHARE row lock. That was a harness fault, not a product fault; the unhandled 40001 in that log already showed fail-closed behaviour. The new bu-hierarchy-guard.test.ts (7) and migrate.test.ts (9 migrations) pass in both integration runs. Residuals (not findings): the REPEATABLE READ depth-only residual is stated in the migration header; a direct-SQL writer that interleaves a row lock with the trigger can hit 40P01, which fails closed.

findings.title: Business-unit re-parenting authorizes only the moved unit, never the destination parent: a unit-scoped manager moves a unit into a sibling branch it has no rights on, exposing its records to that branch
findings.reproduction: apps/api/src/modules/organization/routes.ts:329-333 runs requireRead(business_unit.read) + requireAction(business_unit.manage) on the unit being moved; :338-365 validate the new parent (same organization, no cycle, depth) but never call authorize/requireAction on the destination parent. Inputs (seedWorld: org A with sibling BUs a1 (child a1x) and a2): user U holds ADM_TECH (business_unit.manage, structural so it applies downward) at BU a1 only; user V holds AUD (inherits downward, transformation.read) at BU a2 only; a transformation exists under a1x. U PATCH /api/v1/business-units/{a2} -> 404 (control: U has no rights on a2). V GET /api/v1/transformations/{tx} -> 404. U PATCH /api/v1/business-units/{a1x} {parentBusinessUnitId: a2} If-Match "1" -> 200. V GET /api/v1/transformations/{tx} -> 200; U GET /api/v1/business-units/{a1x} -> 404. Reproduction (real API, disposable PostgreSQL 16): docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/code-security/round-1/repro-bu/zz-review-bu-hierarchy.test.ts (SEC-2), log repro-bu/repro-bu.log.
findings.expected: A move needs business_unit.manage on the destination parent as well as on the moved unit (or organization-scope business_unit.manage for any move), refused 403/404 otherwise with an audited authorization.denied, consistent with ADR-0006 'grants never apply across siblings' and the CLAUDE.md rule that every mutation is authorized server-side on what it changes.
findings.actual: The move succeeds (200). A manager scoped to a1 writes into a2's subtree, which it has no rights on. a2's inheriting users gain read access to a1x's transformation records (404 -> 200), and a1's own grant holders lose access, all without any authorization on a2.

findings.fix_summary: Re-parent now authorizes business_unit.manage on the destination parent (or the organization for a top-level move) in addition to the moved unit; 403 + denied-mutation audit. Negative test proves the cross-branch exposure is gone.

verification.note: Fixed. apps/api/src/modules/organization/routes.ts now calls requireAction(business_unit.manage) on the destination: on the organization for a top-level move (:370-377) and on the new parent business unit (:389-398). This runs before the cycle/depth checks; the moved unit is still authorized at :359. Re-ran my round-1 repro UNCHANGED (repro-bu/round1-repro-rerun.log). Round-2 repro R2-7 (repro-r2-bu.log): sibling a2 403 forbidden with exactly 1 authorization.denied audit row on a2 ('requires business_unit.manage'); a unit deeper in the sibling branch 403; top level 403; parent unchanged (still a1, version 1); the a2 auditor still 404; the legitimate in-scope move under a1x 200. A destination in another organization gives 422 business_unit.parent_invalid, identical to a nonexistent id, so there is no cross-organization existence oracle.

findings.title: Global rate limit is bypassed by rotating an invalid session cookie: the limiter keys on any presented cookie value, so each fake cookie gets a fresh bucket
findings.reproduction: apps/api/src/server.ts:128-131 keyGenerator returns `s:${sha256(cookie)}` whenever a session cookie is present, without checking that it is a live session, and falls back to the IP only when no cookie is sent. Inputs: RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=3; one client IP (203.0.113.7). Six GET /api/v1/me without a cookie -> 401,401,401,429,429,429 (control). Fifty GET /api/v1/me from the same IP, each with Cookie: mth_session=<fresh random 43-char base64url> -> 50 x 401, never 429. Each such request passes the token-format regex and performs a session lookup in PostgreSQL (identity/routes.ts:107-122, sessions.ts:76). Reproduction: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/code-security/round-1/repro-ratelimit/zz-review-ratelimit.test.ts, log repro-ratelimit/repro-ratelimit.log. The auth routes' own limiter (identity/routes.ts:80-84, keyed by IP) is NOT affected.
findings.expected: An unauthenticated client cannot escape the per-IP budget: key by session only after the session resolved (e.g. a per-IP pre-limit, or key = IP for requests whose cookie does not resolve to a live session), so a flood of fake cookies is limited like cookieless traffic.
findings.actual: Unlimited unauthenticated requests per IP (each costing a SHA-256 and a DB query), contrary to the ADR-0007 rate-limit control described in server.ts:6 and the identity hook comment 'floods are rejected before any DB lookup'.

history.note: raised by code-security-reviewer DG1 round 1 (proposed ID; the orchestrator may renumber)

findings.fix_summary: Rate limiter keys on u:<userId> for a validated session (SHA-256 of the token in a bounded TTL map written only by the identity module) else ip:<request.ip> (TRUST_PROXY-aware); never a raw cookie. Test proves cookie rotation no longer resets the bucket.

verification.note: Fixed. apps/api/src/server.ts keyGenerator returns u:<userId> only when RateLimitSubjects.subjectOf(token) finds the token. Only the identity hook fills that map, after resolveSession succeeds (identity/routes.ts remember/forget). Otherwise it returns ip:<request.ip>; Fastify derives the IP and applies TRUST_PROXY. rate-limit-subjects.ts keys entries by SHA-256 of the token, bounds them (50,000, oldest evicted) with a TTL equal to the idle timeout, and forgets a token on failed resolution, logout or rotation. Re-ran my round-1 repro UNCHANGED (repro-ratelimit/zz-review-ratelimit.log): the bypass test now sees {"429":50}, so its 'never 429' expectation fails. Round-2 repro (zz-review-r2-ratelimit.log, 4/4 PASS, RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=3): RL-1 a fresh random cookie per request from one IP gives 401,401,401 then 429 x17; RL-2 rotating X-Forwarded-For without TRUST_PROXY still gives 429 from the 4th request; RL-3 two sessions of one user from two IPs share one u: bucket (the 4th request is 429); RL-4 a fake-cookie flood that exhausts an IP's bucket does not starve a valid session from that IP (200); RL-5 a logged-out cookie falls back to the IP bucket (401 x3, then 429).

findings.title: Module dependency-lint bypass via the allow-listed third-party dependency ajv: its public codegen tag `_` evaluates arbitrary JS (deep import past access/index.ts, non-allow-listed built-ins) with zero lint violations; ajv/ajv-formats/yaml are test-only yet are runtime dependencies
findings.reproduction: apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts:106-109 allow-lists EVERY runtime dependency of @mth/api (THIRD_PARTY) with any subpath (bareAllowed :195-200). The F-DG1-124 blanket ban (header :22-27, 'every way to reach a primitive needs one of them') and the member audit (:64-78) cover only Node built-ins. ajv (apps/api/package.json:30) compiles validators with new Function, and its exported `_` tag emits the raw literal parts of a template as code. A module file with `import Ajv, { _ } from "ajv"; ajv.addKeyword({ keyword: "x", code(cxt) { cxt.gen.code(_`globalThis.__r = { cp: typeof process.getBuiltinModule("node:child_process").execFileSync, deep: import(${deepPath}) }`) } }); ajv.compile({ x: true })(1);` gives fileViolations() -> []. The real architecture suite stays green (132/132), eslint and the @mth/api typecheck are clean, and at runtime it reaches child_process.execFileSync and deep-imports access/policy.ts (exports authorize, loadGrants, ...). Files: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/code-security/round-1/repro-ajv/zz-ajv-planted.ts and run-repro.mjs, log repro-ajv/repro-ajv.log (planted only in a disposable copy). grep shows ajv, ajv-formats and yaml are imported only by tests (apps/api/test/support/contract.ts, src/modules/admin/branding.test.ts), yet they are `dependencies`, so they are on the module allow-list and are installed into the production image (deploy/scripts/assemble-runtime.sh:40 `--prod`).
findings.expected: Either the testkit header lists third-party code generators as a stated residual, or (better) ajv/ajv-formats/yaml move to devDependencies (off the module allow-list and out of the production image), and the third-party allow-list becomes per-package reviewed (the same default-deny and member-audit treatment as node: built-ins).
findings.actual: A route to arbitrary code evaluation and cross-module deep imports that is neither caught nor a stated residual (the D-053 reopen criterion), plus three test-only packages shipped as production runtime dependencies. Same class and calibration as F-DG1-124..133 (Low): static defence-in-depth over human-reviewed code, not a runtime boundary.

findings.fix_summary: ajv/ajv-formats/yaml moved to devDependencies (verified first-party test-only; they remain transitive fastify runtime deps, documented); module-source imports now flagged by the lint. Testkit header states the first-party scope (D-055); self-check added.

verification.note: Fixed. apps/api/package.json moves ajv 8.17.1, ajv-formats 3.0.1 and yaml 2.8.1 to devDependencies. architecture.testkit.ts THIRD_PARTY = dependencies only; TEST_ONLY_THIRD_PARTY (devDependencies minus @types, plus vitest) is allowed only for *.test.ts/*.test.tsx. The SCOPE header honestly limits the lint to first-party source. Re-ran my round-1 plant UNCHANGED in the disposable clone (repro-ajv/repro-ajv-rerun.log): fileViolations reports 'imports package ajv' twice, and the real ADR-0002 suite now FAILS with the plant present (exit 1), so pnpm test / CI refuses it. The import still executes locally only because the dev install contains ajv. That is expected, because the control is the lint gate. 13 import-form variants (static, subpath, dynamic, template dynamic, export *, named re-export, type-only, import = require, require(), ajv-formats, yaml, @fastify/ajv-compiler, and a *.test.mts that ships in dist) are all flagged (variants.log, UNFLAGGED=0). Framing check: pnpm-lock.yaml confirms ajv and ajv-formats remain transitive RUNTIME deps of fastify@5.6.1 (via @fastify/ajv-compiler 4.0.6 and fast-json-stringify 6.4.0), and licenses/inventory.csv keeps them 'runtime, apps/api (dev)'. That is honest. yaml is NOT a fastify runtime dep (only vite/vitest use it), and the inventory correctly reclassifies it as 'development'; the assignment's shorthand 'they remain transitive fastify runtime deps' is accurate only for ajv/ajv-formats. SBOM --check is OK (sbom-check.log).

findings.title: Three database views created by the P1 migrations (actor_display, business_unit_closure, scope_node) are not documented in the data dictionary or the ERD
findings.reproduction: In a disposable clone of candidate sha256:25c97340… (commit 37ec374): tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh bash docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/qa/round-1/26-schema-vs-dictionary.sh. This migrates a fresh PostgreSQL 16 database and compares information_schema.columns (schema public) with the '## <table>' sections of docs/architecture/data-dictionary.md. Then run: grep -niE 'closure|view|scope_node|actor_display' docs/architecture/data-dictionary.md docs/architecture/erd.md. The views are created in packages/db/migrations/0001_identity_access.sql:62 (actor_display) and :93 (business_unit_closure, a recursive view capped at depth < 10), and in 0002_transformation.sql:48 (scope_node, GRANT SELECT to mth_app). The access policy uses business_unit_closure and scope_node (apps/api/src/modules/access/policy.ts, assignments.ts).

findings.title: Non-deterministic e2e journey: 'shell: navigation, language persistence and My Work' presses Tab before the shell has mounted after page.reload(), so the skip-link toBeFocused assertion intermittently fails (1 of 29 normal runs; 1 of 15 under CPU load) and, because the spec is serial, skips the remaining 7 journeys of that locale
findings.reproduction: Disposable clone of candidate sha256:e6979e12… (commit 485e91f), Node v22.22.2, PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers. (1) E2E_PG_PORT=55941 apps/web/e2e/support/with-stack.sh npx playwright test apps/web/e2e --workers=1 --reporter=list -> 1 failed, 7 did not run, 10 passed, exit 1 ([chromium-en] journeys.spec.ts:156, line 172: expect(getByRole('link', {name: 'Skip to main content'})).toBeFocused() -> Received: inactive, 9x over 5000 ms). (2) With three parallel `pnpm test` runs as CPU load on the 4-CPU host: apps/web/e2e/support/with-stack.sh npx playwright test apps/web/e2e/journeys.spec.ts -g 'shell: navigation' --project=chromium-en --repeat-each=15 --workers=1 -> 1 failed / 14 passed, same assertion. Without load: two more full suite runs 18/18, the qa-stack run 22/22, and --repeat-each=10 over both locales 20/20. Root cause (test synchronisation, not a product defect): after `await page.reload()` the test only waits for `html[lang]`, but `public/locale-boot.js` sets <html lang dir> before first paint, i.e. before React has mounted the shell. The Tab keypress can therefore land while no focusable element exists; in the failure snapshot the skip link (first focusable element) is present afterwards but unfocused (screenshot shows the fully rendered My Work page with nothing focused).
findings.expected: A required gate check (master prompt §0: required checks run and pass; playwright.config.ts retries: 0, so CI is red on any flake) that is deterministic: after the reload, wait for a post-mount signal (e.g. the primary navigation or the My Work heading to be visible) before pressing Tab, as the earlier part of the same test already does after sign-in.
findings.actual: Intermittent failure of the required e2e journeys check (first run of this review: exit 1, 7 EN journeys not executed). The product behaviour itself is correct in every run where the shell had mounted (skip link is the first focusable element; 28 of 29 unloaded runs and 14 of 15 loaded runs pass).

findings.title: The Playwright e2e specs (apps/web/e2e/**, playwright.config.ts) are outside every typecheck target, so the changed journeys.spec.ts is never type-checked by any gate or CI step
findings.reproduction: apps/web/tsconfig.json:14 has "include": ["src", "test", "vite.config.ts", "vitest.config.ts"]. There is no root tsconfig.json (only tsconfig.base.json) and no apps/web/e2e/tsconfig*.json, so `pnpm -r typecheck` (which runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json` per package) never compiles apps/web/e2e/journeys.spec.ts or playwright.config.ts. Playwright transpiles specs without type-checking, and ESLint (which does cover the file) does not report type errors. Failure scenario: a spec change such as passing a wrong type to a helper (e.g. `expectShellReadyForKeyboard(page, nav, lang)` with arguments swapped, or calling a non-existent Locator method on a branch not reached in a given run) passes typecheck, lint and the CI typecheck job, and is only caught (or not) at e2e run time. The reviewer type-checked the round-3 change with a disposable tsconfig outside the candidate (ES2023 + DOM lib, types node): it passes (exit 0), so this is a coverage gap, not a current defect. Evidence: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/code-security/round-3/e2e-spec-typecheck.log.
findings.expected: The e2e specs and playwright.config.ts are type-checked by `pnpm -r typecheck` and so by CI, e.g. through an apps/web/e2e/tsconfig.json (lib ES2023 + DOM, types node) referenced from apps/web's typecheck script or from a root typecheck step.
findings.actual: No typecheck target includes apps/web/e2e/**. A type error in the e2e specs passes every static gate check. The current spec type-checks cleanly when the reviewer checks it ad hoc.

findings.title: Evidence separation of duties is bypassable: a reviewer can verify content they wrote or uploaded themselves on evidence another user created, because the rule only compares the reviewer with the row's created_by
findings.reproduction: apps/api/src/modules/evidence/routes.ts:388 (and CHECK evidence_verified_rule, packages/db/migrations/0012_p2_evidence.sql:46) refuse the review only when reviewer = evidence.created_by. But PATCH /evidence/{id} (routes.ts:107, writeRules CREATE = evidence.create with scope 'any') and POST /evidence/{id}/content (routes.ts:295-340, same rule, uploaded_by = caller) let ANY evidence.create holder replace another user's note text, URL or file bytes. Both operations reset the review and leave created_by unchanged. Inputs (synthetic): WL creates note evidence E. TL sends PATCH E {noteBody: <TL's own text>} with If-Match "1" and gets 200. TL then sends POST E/review {result: verified, accessibilityStatus: accessible} and gets 200 verified with reviewedBy = TL. The file variant works the same way: WL creates file evidence F, TL uploads revision 1 (uploaded_by = TL), TL verifies it and gets 200, reviewedContentId = TL's own upload. TL, BO and TO all hold both evidence.create and evidence.review (packages/shared/src/permissions.ts). A single TL can therefore supply AND verify the 'VERIFIED evidence' that the g1.diagnostic / g1.baseline criteria (workflows/criteria.ts) require, then submit G1. Reproduced through the API on a disposable PostgreSQL 16, in 2 runs: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/code-security/round-1/probes/zz-sec-r1-probe.test.ts (SEC-1), probe-run1.log and probe-run2.log.
findings.expected: Nobody verifies evidence content they supplied: the review is refused (403) when the reviewer is the creator, the author of the current note/URL text, or the uploader of the current content revision (or the rule is bound to the content author, e.g. reviewed_by <> uploaded_by / last content editor, enforced in the API and in the CHECK/trigger). Editing or replacing another user's evidence content should also be limited (own rows, or an explicit edit permission).
findings.actual: 200 verified in both variants. SEC-1.note: [200,"verified",reviewedBy=TL]. SEC-1.file: [200,"verified",reviewedContentId = the TL's own upload]. The DB CHECK passes because created_by is still the WL.

findings.title: T02 target-trajectory approval (kpi_target.approve, a business_approval) is bypassable: a Business Owner can change another user's target value and then approve the trajectory they just set
findings.reproduction: apps/api/src/modules/kpi/outcome-kpis.ts:289 (and CHECK outcome_kpi_approver_not_creator, packages/db/migrations/0014_p2_kpi_baseline_value_pool.sql:120) refuse approval only when approver = outcome_kpi.created_by. BO holds BOTH outcome.edit (the PATCH permission, outcome-kpis.ts:45/162) and kpi_target.approve (packages/shared/src/permissions.ts:100-108). Inputs (synthetic): TL creates a T02 row with targetValue "100" and gets 201. BO sends PATCH {targetValue: "5"} and gets 200 (trajectory back to draft, created_by still TL). BO sends POST .../trajectory-approval with If-Match = the new version and gets 200 trajectoryStatus approved, trajectoryApprovedBy = BO. The approved trajectory then satisfies the g2.target_trajectory criterion (workflows/criteria.ts) for G2 submission. Reproduced through the API on a disposable PostgreSQL 16, in 2 runs: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/code-security/round-1/probes/zz-sec-r1-probe.test.ts (SEC-2), probe-run1.log and probe-run2.log.
findings.expected: A business approval is never given by the person who authored the approved content: approval is refused (403) when the approver last changed the target/trajectory (for example, by comparing with updated_by of the current version or keeping a target-author column), as well as when the approver is the row's creator. The DB CHECK should enforce the same rule.
findings.actual: SEC-2: bo_sets_target [200,"5.000000"], then bo_approves_own_target [200,"approved",trajectoryApprovedBy=BO].

findings.title: Evidence-link removal skips the record-level edit check that link creation requires: any evidence.create holder can remove any link, including links that satisfy gate criteria
findings.reproduction: POST /transformations/{id}/evidence-links requires edit rights on the linked record (apps/api/src/modules/evidence/routes.ts:496, RECORD_WRITE_RULES, ADR-0018 §4). POST .../evidence-links/{linkId}/remove (routes.ts:539-585) only calls openWrite(..., CREATE = evidence.create). It loads the link's created_by (routes.ts:546) and never uses it, and applies no RECORD_WRITE_RULES check. Inputs (synthetic): TL links verified evidence to a seeded T01 diagnostic_item and gets 201. WL (diagnostic.contribute is own-rows only) tries the same link and is refused with 403, as designed. The same WL sends POST /evidence-links/{TL's link}/remove {reason} with If-Match "1" and gets 200, status removed. Removing the only verified link makes g1.diagnostic incomplete, so a contributor can silently un-ready (or, after submission, alter the live readiness of) a gate. Reproduced through the API on a disposable PostgreSQL 16, in 2 runs: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/code-security/round-1/probes/zz-sec-r1-probe.test.ts (SEC-3), probe-run1.log and probe-run2.log.
findings.expected: Removing a link needs the same authorization as creating it (edit rights on the target record, through requireRecordWrite with RECORD_WRITE_RULES), otherwise 403 with a denied-mutation audit event.
findings.actual: SEC-3: {"wlCreateStatus":403,"tlCreateStatus":201,"wlRemoveStatus":200,"after":"removed"}

findings.title: G2 Direction can never be completed through native workflows: every KPI definition stays 'draft' (no API or UI path sets 'active'), and the G2 criterion g2.kpi_definitions requires an ACTIVE definition, so G2 can never be submitted or approved and the Diagnose->Define->Design journey cannot complete (also REQ-S04-004, REQ-DLV-034)
findings.reproduction: Disposable clone of candidate sha256:8ef26b71… (commit 98a8d99), Node v22.22.2, disposable PostgreSQL 16. Copy docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/qa/tests/dg2-qa-journey.test.ts to tests/qa/integration/ and run `QA_PG_PORT=54761 tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh npx vitest run --project integration --reporter=verbose tests/qa/integration/dg2-qa-journey.test.ts`. The test completes every Define output through public API operations only, as the roles of the permissions matrix: North Star (TL), guardrail (TL), KPI definition with unit, polarity and owner (KDS), three top outcomes passing the good outcome test (TL), T02 rows with target, target date, owner, leading indicator and trajectory (KDS), each trajectory approved by the SP. GET /gates/G2 still reports g2.kpi_definitions incomplete with `g2.kpi_definitions.not_active`. PATCH /kpi-definitions/{id} {status:'active'} -> 400 validation; POST /kpi-definitions {..., status:'active'} -> 400 validation; the definition stays 'draft'. Deterministic in 2/2 runs. Static: the 160-operation contract has only list/create/get/update/archive for kpi-definitions; KpiDefinitionUpdate has no `status`; the only status write in apps/api/src/modules/kpi/kpi-definitions.ts sets 'archived'; no migration trigger activates a definition. criteria.ts:367-370 requires `d.status === 'active'`.
findings.expected: REQ-PB-017 / REQ-S04-004: G2 links North Star, the T02 tree, KPI definitions and guardrails, and can be submitted and decided once they are complete. REQ-DLV-034: a full Diagnose->Design journey (business gates G1-G3) completes through native workflows. A gate criterion must be satisfiable by a native user action, such as activating a KPI definition by KDS or TL, or the criterion must accept a complete definition.
findings.actual: G2 is permanently incomplete (`g2.kpi_definitions.not_active`). `canSubmit` stays false and submission returns 422 gate_criteria_incomplete, so G2 can never be approved and the transformation can only reach Design by a direct DB write. The existing integration and e2e suites only ever submit and decide G1, so this was not caught.

findings.title: Scope sanity check 'Are explicit exclusions documented?' (B0041) never fails: an empty Out of scope on a saved charter gives 'unknown', and a whitespace-only Out of scope gives 'pass'
findings.reproduction: Disposable clone at eb8163e2 (candidate 089a2a2f…), fresh PostgreSQL 16 and API (AUTH_MODE=dev, synthetic seed), Node 24.21.0: `with-stack.sh node live-scenario.mjs`. As dev.lead: POST /api/v1/transformations (end_to_end), then POST /transformations/{id}/charter with name, sponsor, lead, case for change, in scope and baseline date but no outOfScope. GET /charter returns scopeCheckPrechecks[exclusions_documented] = {result:'unknown', detail:'No exclusions (out of scope) are recorded yet.'}. Then PATCH /charter {outOfScope:'   '} returns 200, stores '   ', and the same pre-check returns 'pass' ('Explicit exclusions are documented.'). The charter screen renders the 'unknown' state as a grey 'Unknown' badge and the whitespace case as green 'Supported by data'. Source: apps/api/src/modules/transformations/charter.ts:250-253 (`c.out_of_scope === null ? unknown : pass`), and packages/shared/src/schemas/charter.ts `outOfScope: text(1, 20000)` (min length counts whitespace). The result enum has 'attention' but this pre-check never uses it.
findings.expected: Register acceptance for REQ-PB-031: 'an empty Out of scope field makes 'Are explicit exclusions documented?' fail'. On a saved charter the Out of scope field is known to be empty (charter field B0035 'Out of scope: [Explicit exclusions]'), so the B0041 check fails, for example with the 'attention' result and a reason. A blank or whitespace-only value is not a documented exclusion and must not pass.
findings.actual: Empty Out of scope gives 'unknown' (neutral grey, not a failure), and whitespace-only gives 'pass' (green). The check can therefore never fail, and the assigned acceptance criterion is not met. ADR-0017 §2 ('missing data gives unknown') is applied to a field whose emptiness is itself the B0041 answer.

findings.title: Invisible-only free text (U+0085 NEL, zero-width and bidi format characters) passes freeText() and counts as present in hasText(), so the B0041 exclusions pre-check reads 'pass' and G1 treats Out of scope as documented (residual of the F-DG2-150 / D-063 class)
findings.reproduction: packages/shared/src/schemas/common.ts:42 (hasText) and :58 (freeText refine) both decide blankness with String.prototype.trim(). That strips only ECMAScript WhiteSpace/LineTerminator, not U+0085 NEXT LINE (a Unicode White_Space code point) or Cf format characters such as U+200B ZWSP, U+200C/U+200D, U+2060 WORD JOINER, U+200F RLM, U+061C ARABIC LETTER MARK (the bidi marks are common in Arabic RTL input). Schema matrix (schema-unicode-matrix.log): freeText(1,100) ACCEPTS and hasText returns true for U+0085, U+180E, U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+2060, U+3164, U+2800, U+00AD, U+061C, U+200F; it correctly rejects NBSP, U+3000, U+2028, U+FEFF, U+2007. End to end (disposable clone at 9e13947e, disposable PostgreSQL 16, zz-sec-r3-invisible.test.ts, 2 runs): POST /api/v1/transformations/{id}/charter by the Transformation Lead with outOfScope = '\u0085' (or '\u200b', '\u200f', '\u061c', '\u2060\u2060\u2060') -> 201 and stored. GET .../charter -> scopeCheckPrechecks exclusions_documented = 'pass' ('Explicit exclusions are documented.'). GET .../gates/G1 -> g1.initial_charter does not list /charter/outOfScope as missing (apps/api/src/modules/workflows/criteria.ts:172 via hasExclusions, apps/api/src/modules/transformations/charter.ts:219-220 and :264).
findings.expected: Per D-063 ('blank free text is rejected on every P2 input and never counts as present in G1-G3 readiness') and B0041, text with no visible content is not a documented exclusion. Either freeText rejects it with 400 validation.blank (nothing written, no audit), or hasText treats it as not present. For example, test /[^\p{White_Space}\p{Cf}]/u (plus U+3164/U+2800/U+115F/U+1160 if desired) instead of trim(), in the one shared helper so API, pre-checks and web stay consistent.
findings.actual: An Out of scope that renders as empty is accepted (201), and the B0041 pre-check and the G1 initial-charter criterion both treat it as documented exclusions. findings.title: Web forms silently turn whitespace-only text into null: the localized validation__blank message (D-063) is unreachable, and a blank save creates a charter, a content-free charter version, or clears an existing Out of scope
findings.reproduction: Disposable clone @9e13947e, real built SPA + API + PostgreSQL (e2e/support/qa-stack.sh with a port parameter only), chromium-en and chromium-ar, spec docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/qa/tests/round-3/e2e/dg2-qa-blank-r3.spec.ts, run twice. (1) Charter > Create charter, Case for change = '   \t  ', Create: no message; GET charter -> 200 v1 with caseForChange null. (2) Charter with Out of scope null > Edit charter, Out of scope = whitespace, change summary filled, Save version: no message; a new charter version v2 is saved (probe dg2-qa-blank-probe-r3.spec.ts shows the PATCH body is {"changeSummary":"QA probe"} only and versions [[2,'QA probe'],[1,null]]). (3) Charter with Out of scope 'Enterprise contracts (synthetic)' > Edit, replace it with whitespace, Save version: no message; v2 -> v3 with outOfScope null, i.e. the documented exclusion is cleared. (4) Diagnose > T01 Edit, Current state = whitespace, Save draft: no blank message; the dialog shows 'There are no changes to save.' / 'لا توجد تغييرات لحفظها.' Cause: apps/web/src/components/RecordForm.tsx fromFormValue (default branch) maps s.trim() === '' to null before the request, so the server's 400 validation.blank is never triggered from these forms. The web unit test 'Diagnose a 400 validation.blank shows a localized message on its field' mocks the 400 and therefore does not exercise this path.
findings.expected: Per D-063 ('The web shows the EN/AR validation__blank message') and the round-3 assignment: whitespace-only text in a charter field or a T01 field shows the localized blank-validation message (EN/AR) and saves nothing. No charter is created, no charter version is written, and an existing value is not cleared by typing spaces.
findings.actual: In EN and AR, in both runs, the blank message is never shown. Whitespace is treated as an empty field: create saves a charter without the field; edit saves a new charter version with no content change, or clears an existing Out of scope (the exclusions chip then correctly fails). T01 shows 'no changes to save'. Data integrity holds: blank text is never stored, and readiness and pre-checks stay correct (hard assertions pass).

history.note: Raised by qa-verifier in DG2 round 3 (T-DG2-REV-QA-R3) from the assignment's own negative UI check, which fails in EN and AR in two runs. findings.title: RecordForm error banner <ul role="alert"> breaks list semantics: axe reports a serious 'listitem' violation (EN and AR) whenever the banner is shown

findings.title: OIDC just-in-time display name is cut to 200 code units AFTER the visible-content check, so a name claim of 200 invisible characters followed by visible text is stored as an invisible display name
findings.reproduction: apps/api/src/modules/identity/oidc.ts:167: `if (typeof v === "string" && hasText(v)) return v.trim().slice(0, 200);`. The visible-content test runs on the whole claim, but the stored value is the first 200 UTF-16 code units. On a disposable clone at e37f6ea4 with the candidate's local fake OpenID Provider and a disposable PostgreSQL 16 (zz-sec-r4-oidc.test.ts test 2, 2 runs), a first sign-in with sub 'r4-sub-2', preferred_username 'r4.second' and name = '\u200b' x 200 + 'Visible Synthetic' gets a 302, and JIT creates app_user.display_name of length 200 with hasText(display_name) = false. findings.expected: The display name chosen at JIT provisioning has visible content, consistent with the F-DG2-160 intent of this change (an invisible name claim is treated as absent). findings.actual: The user is created with a display name that renders as empty wherever people are shown (owners, approvers, audit actor names), until an administrator renames them. Identity, session and authorization are unaffected: binding is by (iss, sub), no scoped assignment is created, and test 1 of the same probe confirms a second login signs in the same user.

findings.title: U+0000 (NUL) inside otherwise visible free text passes validation and reaches PostgreSQL, which rejects it (SQLSTATE 22021); the API answers with an undeclared 500 Internal error instead of a 400 validation problem
findings.reproduction: freeText, name and reason (packages/shared/src/schemas/common.ts:77-103) check length and visible content only. A value such as 'Synthetic\u0000exclusion' has visible content, so it is accepted (a NUL-only value is rejected since F-DG2-180, because Cc is excluded). PostgreSQL text cannot hold NUL. (1) My three round-5 repros (zz-sec-r5-nul.test.ts, rerun unchanged) now PASS in both runs: charter outOfScope 'Synthetic\u0000exclusion', transformation name 'Synthetic\u0000name' and TOM gap archive reason 'Synthetic\u0000reason' each get a 4xx (400 validation.invalid_character at /outOfScope, /name or /reason). For a signed-in caller without the permission, the 400 comes before the handler's authorization. The status is the same whether or not the transformation exists (400/400), so it is not an existence oracle, and nothing is written. That matches the existing pre-authorization 400 for malformed JSON. It does not reject legitimate input: '\\0', '%00', '\\u0000' as literal text, U+0001 and U+FFFD are stored verbatim. Only callback opts out (invalidCharacters: 'route' appears once). contract.test.ts includes 'every operation but the OIDC callback: U+0000 in the query is a declared 400' and the 161-operation assertion; it passes in both integration runs, as does invalid-character.test.ts (13/13). The (iss, sub) binding, no roles at JIT, a working session and the single-use login cookie are all unchanged. findings.title: A lone UTF-16 surrogate in the ID token's sub makes the OIDC callback answer an undeclared 400 problem (validation.format) instead of its declared 302 redirect, and the failed sign-in leaves no audit row
findings.reproduction: A lone surrogate is legal in a JSON string escape ('\ud800'), so it survives JSON.parse of the ID token payload. identityClaimsStorable (apps/api/src/modules/identity/oidc.ts) checks only for U+0000. resolveOidcUser inserts user_identity (text: node-postgres sends UTF-8, so the column would receive U+FFFD). It then audits changes { identity: { issuer, subject } } through packages/db/src/audit.ts, whose changes column is JSON.stringify(event.changes). JSON.stringify keeps the lone surrogate as the escape '\ud800', PostgreSQL's jsonb input refuses that escape with SQLSTATE 22P02, and apps/api/src/modules/platform/hooks.ts maps 22P02 to 400 validation.format. Probe: disposable clone at 51a692b1, disposable PostgreSQL 16.13, the candidate's FakeIdp; zz-sec-r6-surrogate.test.ts, run with LANG unset (surrogate-probe-run1.log) and with LANG=C.UTF-8 (probe-run2.log). GET /api/v1/auth/callback with a valid code whose ID token has sub 'r6s-jit-\ud800' (JIT path), or sub 'r6s-bind-\udfff' plus a verified e-mail of a pre-provisioned user (bind path), returns 400 application/problem+json {code: validation, errors: [{pointer: '', code: 'validation.format'}]}. The harness contract check reports 'completeOidcLogin does not declare status 400 (declared: 302, 429)'. The audit_event rows for the request id: none. No identity or session is created, and the login cookie is cleared.
findings.expected: The callback contract (docs/api/openapi.yaml completeOidcLogin: 302, 429; ADR-0007 §5a names it as the only operation without a 400) is honoured for every ID token. A subject or issuer the server cannot store or audit faithfully is refused like the NUL case: 302 /login?error=token_invalid, with a session.login_failed audit row. For example, extend identityClaimsStorable to refuse lone surrogates (e.g. !iss.isWellFormed() || !sub.isWellFormed(), Node 20+), or map the callback's database errors to its declared redirect. Add an oidc.test.ts case. Optionally, apply the same well-formedness check in hasInvalidCharacter so that free text is not silently rewritten to U+FFFD.
findings.actual: Undeclared 400 problem JSON from a browser-navigation endpoint (the user sees a raw JSON error page instead of the login page), and a failed sign-in with no audit row. Integrity and confidentiality hold: the transaction rolls back, no user, identity or session is created, and the body carries only a requestId. On the main API, lone surrogates in free text never give a 5xx (the text columns store U+FFFD; a value that reaches jsonb directly, e.g. a journey step name, gets a declared 400 validation.format at pointer ''), so this is limited to the callback.

history.note: Raised by code-security-reviewer, DG2 round 6, while probing for residuals of the F-DG2-231 class as assigned. Low and non-mandatory, the same rating as F-DG2-231. The input is IdP-issued: it needs the trusted OpenID Provider to sign an ID token whose sub contains a lone surrogate (Keycloak subjects are UUIDs), so an end user cannot trigger it. No integrity, authorization or confidentiality impact: everything rolls back and nothing internal leaks. It is a contract and audit-completeness defect. It does not block the round. findings.title: A JSON request body with invalid UTF-8 bytes gets an undeclared 500 internal, before authentication, when it has a Content-Length; sent chunked, it is silently stored and audited as U+FFFD
findings.reproduction: Fastify 5.6.1 rawBody (node_modules fastify/lib/contentTypeParser.js:222-290) reads a JSON body with payload.setEncoding('utf8'). Each invalid UTF-8 sequence becomes U+FFFD, which is 3 bytes, so the decoded byte count differs from Content-Length. Fastify then raises FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_CONTENT_LENGTH (statusCode 400), shown by fastify-errcode.log. apps/api/src/modules/platform/hooks.ts mapError (lines 54-80) has no case for that code, so setErrorHandler (lines 142-149) logs 'unhandled error' at error level and answers 500 internal. Body parsing runs before the preValidation authentication hook (apps/api/src/modules/identity/routes.ts:120), so no session is needed. Probe: disposable clone at 90439483, disposable PostgreSQL 16, zz-sec-r7-probe.test.ts part B, identical results with LANG unset (probe-run1-lang-unset.log) and LANG=C.UTF-8 (probe-run2-lang-c-utf8.log). (B1) POST /api/v1/transformations/{id}/charter as the Transformation Lead, body {"transformationName":"Synthetic","outOfScope":"Synthetic<bytes> text"}: the control byte 0x41 gives 201; bytes ED A0 80 (CESU-8 lone surrogate), FF or C3 each give 500 {type: urn:mth:problem:internal, code: internal, requestId}. Nothing is stored or audited. (B2) The same body over a real socket with no cookie and no CSRF token: the control gives 401; byte FF gives 500 internal, not 401. (B3) The same body sent with Transfer-Encoding: chunked (no Content-Length), authenticated: 201, charter.out_of_scope is stored as 'Synthetic\uFFFD text', and the charter.create audit_event changes holds U+FFFD. Every operation with a JSON body is affected, because the parser and error mapping are shared.
findings.expected: Every operation's contract is honoured for every request body. A body that is not valid UTF-8 (RFC 8259 §8.1) is refused with the declared 400 ValidationError, as invalid JSON already is (validation.json via FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_JSON_BODY), whatever the framing. The text is never silently rewritten to U+FFFD: that is the same faithfulness rule F-DG2-260 applied to lone surrogates in JSON escapes. One fix: register the application/json parser with parseAs 'buffer' and decode with new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true }), mapping a decode failure to 400 (e.g. validation.json or validation.encoding). In addition, map FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_CONTENT_LENGTH to a 400 problem in mapError. Add an integration case with a Content-Length body and a chunked body, unauthenticated and authenticated.
findings.actual: Undeclared 500 internal for any client that sends ill-formed UTF-8 with a Content-Length, including an unauthenticated one, with an error-level 'unhandled error' log entry each time. With chunked framing, the request is accepted and the replaced text is stored and audited. Integrity and confidentiality hold otherwise: on the 500 path nothing is written, the body carries only a requestId, and the global rate limiter (onRequest) still applies. Browsers' fetch/XHR always send well-formed UTF-8, so the trigger is a non-browser client. By code inspection the behaviour predates this round: neither 51a692b1 nor 90439483 maps the code, and the parser is the framework default. It is not a regression of BE11/BE12.

history.note: Raised by code-security-reviewer, DG2 round 7, during the assigned adversarial probe for strings that are not well-formed. This is the raw-byte counterpart of F-DG2-260 (lone surrogates in JSON escapes, now verified fixed). Low and non-mandatory, the same rating as F-DG2-231 (an undeclared 500 for NUL): it breaks the contract and lands in the error log, but there is no integrity, authorization or confidentiality impact. It is rate-limited and needs a non-browser client. It does not block the round.

findings.fix_summary: BE13 d9c3f5d: application/json is read as raw bytes (parseAs buffer; bodyLimit and the length check apply to raw bytes), decoded with TextDecoder in fatal mode, then parsed by Fastify's default JSON parser. Ill-formed UTF-8 gets the declared 400 validation.json under both Content-Length and chunked framing, never 500 and never U+FFFD; a single BOM is stripped. A strict query-string parser returns 400 validation.format at /query/<key> for an undecodable component. Cookies and headers were swept. ARCH-03 cac0788 declares 429 and every other platform status, so the rate-limit path asserts the contract. Negative controls fail on the old code.

verification.note:
Verified on candidate sha256:9331e9d13e0ffa55f35ebc25ecdf9b60e159876dc2470fe56e9241a40fea124f (source cf3446e4, 539 files). I recomputed it in a disposable clone at cf3446e4 and at HEAD 4053630c, and ran it against disposable PostgreSQL 16 clusters with LANG unset (SQL_ASCII) and LANG=C.UTF-8 (UTF8).
(1) My round-7 repro, zz-sec-r7-probe.test.ts, rerun unchanged, now passes 14/14 in both runs (in round 7: 12 pass, 2 fail):
- B1: charter create with a Content-Length body holding ED A0 80, FF or C3 now gets 400 validation.json at pointer '' (it was 500 internal). There is no charter and no audit row. Control 0x41 still gives 201.
- B2: unauthenticated, over a real socket: 400 validation.json as problem+json (it was a 500). Control: 401.
- B3: chunked and authenticated: 400 (it was 201 with Synthetic\uFFFD text stored and audited). Nothing is stored, and no U+FFFD appears in charter or audit_event.changes.
(2) Code. server.ts registers addContentTypeParser('application/json', { parseAs: 'buffer' }, createJsonBodyParser(app.getDefaultJsonParser('error','error'))).

- parseQueryString (routerOptions.querystringParser) keeps the null-prototype shape and marks undecodable components through a WeakMap. Nothing reassigns request.query, and there is no validatorCompiler that could replace it, so the mark survives until the preHandler check. That check runs after authentication and CSRF, and the OIDC callback (invalidCharacters: 'route') keeps its 302.
(3) Adversarial probe zz-sec-r8-probe.test.ts, both runs:
