- R2: one BOM gives 201 with the exact text. Two BOMs, BOM+FF, a BOM alone, and UTF-16LE/BE bodies give 400. A U+FEFF inside a string is kept verbatim.
- R3: charset=iso-8859-1 or utf-16le never switches the decoder (400). Other +json types give 400 validation.content_type.

- R7: query pointers /query/q, /query, /query/a~0b~1c; a stray % gives 400; '+' and emoji decode; 401 precedes; an unmatched route gives 404; no error log.
- R8: an X-File-Name refusal never precedes authorization: a non-editor gets 403.
- R9: chunked, no session: 400.
- R10: no U+FFFD in charter, audit_event or evidence_content.file_name.
(4) The candidate's own invalid-utf8.test.ts (14 tests) and request-encoding unit tests (18) pass on Node 22 and 24 and in both locales. Cookies and headers stay byte-faithful (Latin-1); the round-7 C1/C2 probes still pass.
The one residual this round found has a different root cause: the evidence upload route accepts text/plain and application/json bodies that its contract does not declare, and the store iterates whatever body it receives. It predates BE13 (same behaviour at 90439483) and is raised separately as F-DG2-320 (Low). This finding's scope and stated remedy, JSON bodies and query strings decoded strictly with a declared 400 in every framing, are fully fixed.

findings.title: Disposable-PostgreSQL test harnesses pick their ports inside the Linux ephemeral range (32768-60999), so a run sporadically fails to start with EADDRINUSE when a just-closed client socket in TIME_WAIT holds that port
findings.reproduction: Clone @90439483, node v24.21.0. Sequential full integration runs through tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh with QA_PG_PORT in the 55xxx/56xxx range. 2 of 12 full-project attempts never started: 10-integration-unset-run2.log (port 55172) and 10-integration-cutf8-load-attempt1.log (port 56402). Both show postgres 'could not bind IPv4 address "127.0.0.1": Address already in use' -> 'BLOCKED: disposable PostgreSQL did not start', exit 3, and no listener was present on the port moments later. Mechanism reproduced in isolation (11-port-collision-repro.py/.log): ip_local_port_range is 32768-60999; a client socket that closes first leaves TIME_WAIT on its ephemeral port, and a later bind+listen on that port, even with SO_REUSEADDR as postgres uses, fails with EADDRINUSE. The default ports of every disposable-cluster harness are inside that range: apps/web/e2e/support/with-stack.sh 54331, deploy/scripts/clean-start-local.sh 54340, tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh 54351, e2e/support/qa-stack.sh 54361. The previous run's many pool and client connections to 127.0.0.1 consume ephemeral ports right next to the next run's port choice. Reruns on the same suite with other ports (2xxxx) passed 531/531.
findings.expected: A disposable test cluster starts deterministically. Its port is outside the kernel's ephemeral range (for example below 32768), or is reserved, or is retried or chosen free at bind time, so an unrelated client TIME_WAIT cannot make a gate run fail at setup.
findings.actual: Sporadic exit 3 'disposable PostgreSQL did not start' (EADDRINUSE) with no product cause. It fails closed (BLOCKED, never a silent pass), so no result is falsified. It does produce unexplained red runs of the kind D-067 records. This mechanism does NOT explain the orchestrator's D-067 symptom (vitest ran, one file failed at setup, 11 skipped), because a bind failure stops before vitest starts. That symptom did not recur in 24 runs containing the two candidate files here (10 full runs, 5 per locale incl. one under CPU load each; 12 targeted loops, 6 per locale; 2 runs with the QA suites), all green with 0 skipped.

history.note: Raised by qa-verifier in DG2 round 7 (T-DG2-REV-QA-R7) because the assignment requires every failed run to be explained and raised. Two of the four harnesses (tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh, e2e/support/qa-stack.sh) are qa-verifier's own; owner devops-engineer as the stack-tooling owner, so qa-verifier does not verify a fix to its own files alone.

findings.fix_summary: DEVOPS3 4e3c446: shared tests/qa/support/pg-port.sh. Default ports for every disposable-cluster harness sit below the Linux ephemeral range (24331/24340/24351/24361/24371). A 3000-connect sample confirms the kernel assigns client ports only in 32768-60999, and every harness default is now below it (24331/24340/24351/24361/24371; APIs 3000/3060/3100/3181), so the natural collision cannot hit a default port. (2) tests/qa/support/port-collision-check.sh: PASS 5/5. C1 still reproduces the defect on the old harness, failing closed. Two concurrent with-pg.sh runs on one port both start, on distinct ports and data dirs. A foreign listener is never adopted. A non-bind startup failure is not retried (BLOCKED, exit 3, command not run). Exhausted retries and *_STRICT_PORT=1 give BLOCKED exit 3. findings.title: uploadEvidenceContent accepts media types its contract does not declare: a chunked text/plain upload stores the file with invalid UTF-8 bytes rewritten to U+FFFD (200, sha256 of the rewritten bytes), and an application/json object or array body gives an undeclared 500
findings.reproduction:
The contract declares only application/octet-stream for POST /api/v1/transformations/{transformationId}/evidence/{evidenceId}/content (docs/api/openapi.yaml, uploadEvidenceContent). apps/api/src/modules/evidence/routes.ts:349 adds an octet-stream parser, but Fastify's default text/plain parser (setEncoding('utf8'): U+FFFD replacement) and the root application/json parser (server.ts) stay registered for the route. The handler casts request.body to AsyncIterable<Uint8Array> | Uint8Array (routes.ts:421). FileSystemEvidenceStore.put (apps/api/src/modules/evidence/store.ts:75-83) then iterates whatever it is given: a string character by character, each one re-encoded as UTF-8; a JSON object, which throws TypeError 'not iterable'; or an array of numbers, where hash.update throws.
Probe: zz-sec-r8-probe.test.ts R6, disposable clone at 4053630c (candidate 9331e9d1), disposable PostgreSQL 16, identical in both runs (probe-run1-lang-unset.log, probe-run2-lang-c-utf8.log). The Transformation Lead creates a file evidence item, then POSTs the content with If-Match, CSRF and X-File-Name:
(a) Content-Type text/plain, chunked (no Content-Length), bytes 53 79 6e ff c3 0a ed a0 80 41: 200. The downloaded content is 53 79 6e ef bf bd ef bf bd 0a ef bf bd ef bf bd ef bf bd 41, and evidence_content.sha256 is the hash of those rewritten bytes, not of the bytes sent.
(b) Content-Type application/json, body {"a":1} or [1,2,3]: 500 urn:mth:problem:internal, not declared for the operation, with an error-level 'unhandled error' log line each time. Nothing is stored and the temp file is removed.
(c) Content-Type application/json, body "Synthetic": 200; the stored content is the JSON-decoded text Synthetic (53796e746865746963), not the 11 bytes sent.
Controls: application/octet-stream with the same ill-formed bytes, with a Content-Length or chunked, is stored and downloaded byte for byte with a matching sha256. text/plain with a Content-Length and invalid bytes now gets 400 validation.malformed_request (BE13's FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_CONTENT_LENGTH mapping).
Baseline: the same R6 at the round-7 candidate 90439483 (probe-r6-baseline-90439483.log) gives the same (a), (b) and (c), and there text/plain with a Content-Length was a 500. So this predates BE13 and is not a regression.
findings.expected: uploadEvidenceContent honours its contract: the request body is application/octet-stream and the stored evidence is exactly the bytes the client sent. Any other media type is refused with the declared 400 ValidationError (validation.content_type, as other operations answer an undeclared media type) before anything is stored, and never gives a 500. This is the F-DG2-290 faithfulness rule (client bytes are never silently rewritten, and never answered with an undeclared status) applied to evidence content. Possible fixes: refuse a request whose Content-Type is not application/octet-stream in the upload route (for example in a route-level preValidation or onRequest hook, or by checking that the body is a stream or Buffer before store.put); or scope the parsers so that only octet-stream reaches this route. Add an integration case for text/plain (both framings) and application/json bodies on this route.
findings.actual: With a non-browser client that labels an upload text/plain and sends it chunked, an evidence file is silently stored with its ill-formed bytes replaced by U+FFFD. The 200 response and the stored sha256 describe the rewritten content, so the upload looks successful while the evidence no longer matches the original. With application/json, an object or array body gives an undeclared 500 plus an error log line, and a JSON string body stores its decoded text. Impact is limited. It needs an authenticated user who passes the route's own ownership check (creator or named owner, EDIT_OWN) and who chooses a media type the contract does not offer. The web client always sends application/octet-stream. No third party can cause it. Authorization, scoping and audit are unaffected, and nothing is stored on the 500 path. It is Low and non-mandatory, the same rating as F-DG2-290, which is the same rewrite class on JSON bodies.

history.note: Raised by code-security-reviewer in DG2 round 8, during the assigned probe for any remaining path where client bytes are silently rewritten or answered with an undeclared status or a 500. It predates BE13 (same behaviour at 90439483), and BE13 improved the text/plain Content-Length case from 500 to 400. Rated Low and non-mandatory like F-DG2-290, because it needs an authorized editor using a non-browser client with an undeclared media type, and has no authorization, confidentiality or audit impact. It does not block the round.

findings.fix_summary: BE14 a7b84d8: each route declares config.consumes (default application/json; uploadEvidenceContent application/octet-stream), checked at registration. One central preParsing hook refuses any other media type with the declared 400 validation.content_type before a body byte is read (after onRequest, so rate limiting still applies). Fastify's text/plain parser is removed; both parsers re-check the route set; the upload handler stores only a raw byte stream. Contract test: every route's set equals its operation's requestBody.content (87 with a body: 86 JSON, 1 octet-stream); live sweep of every undeclared media type on every body-carrying operation; negative control.

verification.note:
Verified on candidate sha256:45ebccc04d8efc0c4fdc6a842eb3c9ec330bab2ec517b1c592af60b05a066294 (source 7854770e, 544 files). I recomputed it in the working tree and in a disposable clone at 7854770e and at HEAD 041478cb, and tested against disposable PostgreSQL 16 clusters with LANG unset (SQL_ASCII) and with LANG=C.UTF-8 (UTF8).
(1) My round-8 repro, zz-sec-r8-probe.test.ts R6, rerun unchanged, now passes in both runs (round 8: FAIL).
- text/plain with a Content-Length, text/plain chunked (with and without NUL, and valid UTF-8 with a charset): each gives 400 validation.content_type. Nothing is stored and nothing is downloadable. Round 8: 200 with EF BF BD rewrites.
- application/json {"a":1} and [1,2,3]: 400 validation.content_type. Round 8: an undeclared 500 plus an error log.
- application/json "Synthetic": 400. Round 8: 200 with the decoded text stored.
- Control: application/octet-stream, with a Content-Length or chunked, is stored and downloaded byte-exact, with sha256 of the bytes sent.
- No error-level log line.
The same repro over a real socket (r9 S8), chunked, with and without a session: 400 validation.content_type; the octet control gives 200 with an exact sha256.
(2) Code (media-types.ts, server.ts, evidence/routes.ts).
- registerMediaTypeEnforcement runs before any route is registered. It removes Fastify's text/plain parser, adds an onRoute check (assertValidConsumes) and adds one root preParsing hook.
- willParseBody mirrors fastify 5.6.1 lib/handleRequest.js. GET, HEAD and TRACE are bodyless. For DELETE, OPTIONS, PATCH, PUT and POST, the parser runs when there is a Content-Type, or when there is none but there is a Transfer-Encoding or a Content-Length other than 0. 5.6.1 has no OPTIONS exception.
- mediaTypeEssence lower-cases and trims the part before ';', using the same single header value Node passes to the parser (r9 S3: with duplicate Content-Type headers Node keeps the first, and the hook and the parser agree).
- Both parsers are wrapped in restrictParserTo. The JSON parser is still parseAs buffer, followed by createJsonBodyParser and Fastify's defaultJsonParser, so bodyLimit, strict UTF-8 and prototype-poisoning protection are unchanged. R1 to R5 still pass.
- The upload handler refuses anything that is not a Uint8Array or an async iterable without readableEncoding. The 25 MiB streaming limit is unchanged (413 evidence.too_large, media-types.test.ts).
- preParsing runs after onRequest (r9 S7, at a 3/min limit: 400 400 400 429 429) and before the preValidation authentication and CSRF checks, as documented. The contract test asserts consumes = requestBody.content for every routed operation (87 with a body: 86 JSON, 1 octet), and the live sweep sends every undeclared type to every body-carrying operation. Both pass in both locales (contract.test.ts 18/18).
(3) Adversarial probe zz-sec-r9-probe.test.ts:
- S1/S2: case, parameter, quoted-charset, list, wildcard, empty, +json, suffix and parameter-smuggling variants never store rewritten bytes. They never give a 500 and are always declared.
- S4: an absent Content-Type with a body gives 400.
- S6: GET/HEAD bodies are never read, and a request smuggled inside a GET chunked body is not executed. I agree with D-069 (a).
- S4: logout and activateKpiDefinition keep JSON-or-nothing; the handlers never read the body; the web client sends no Content-Type without a body. I agree with D-069 (b).
Two residual Low, non-mandatory observations are raised separately because they are outside this finding's reopen condition: no operation accepts an undeclared media type, and nothing is stored rewritten.
- F-DG2-350: an unmatched route given an application/octet-stream body gives 400 instead of 404, a BE14 regression in restrictParserTo.
- F-DG2-351: a Content-Type whose essence is octet-stream but which Fastify's parser lookup cannot match (a tab before ';') is still the declared 400 and stores nothing, but its detail names application/json. This predates BE14.
This finding's scope and stated remedy are fully fixed.

findings.title: A form-level validation problem whose only field error has pointer "" (e.g. the new D-068 validation.json for an invalid-UTF-8 body) is shown twice in RecordForm: the same localized message appears in two role="alert" regions, in English and Arabic
findings.reproduction: Candidate 9331e9d1 (source cf3446e4), qa-stack (real SPA + API + PostgreSQL), chromium-en and chromium-ar. qa-verifier spec docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/qa/tests/round-8/e2e/dg2-qa-r8.spec.ts R8-05: on the charter page, click Create, fill Out of scope, and submit while the browser's POST /charter body carries two invalid UTF-8 bytes (FF FE) inside the value. The real server answers 400 problem+json code validation, errors [{pointer:"", code:"validation.json"}] (correct per D-068). The form then shows 'The request was not valid JSON.' / 'الطلب ليس بصيغة JSON صالحة.' TWICE (screenshots en-/ar-qa-r8-05-charter-invalid-utf8-server.png). Cause (40-f340-duplicate-alert-static.log): in apps/web/src/components/RecordForm.tsx the pointer-"" field error is not mapped to a field, so it goes to `other` (the data-state="form-errors" alert). setBannerError(e) then renders errorMessage(), which in apps/web/src/lib/problem.ts returns the same field-error text for a validation problem whose first error has pointer "" (the data-state="error" alert). The de-duplication on that line only skips codes equal to e.code or validation.<e.code>. The logic dates from bfa1807 (round 4); it is not a D-068 regression. The normal SPA cannot produce such a problem (it always sends valid UTF-8 JSON), so users reach it only through tampered or proxied requests or other pointer-"" validation codes.
findings.expected: One alert per distinct message: a form-level validation problem shows its localized message once (and a screen reader announces it once), in both English LTR and Arabic RTL.
findings.actual: The identical message is rendered in two adjacent role="alert" regions, so it is visually duplicated and announced twice. No data is written, the status and code are correct, and axe reports no serious or critical violation. Polish only.

history.note: Raised by qa-verifier in DG2 round 8 (T-DG2-REV-QA-R8) while regression-testing D-068 in the UI. Low and non-mandatory: a duplicated, correctly localized message on a path the normal SPA does not produce; nothing is written and the server behaviour is correct. Pre-existing RecordForm logic (bfa1807), surfaced by the new validation.json path.

findings.fix_summary: FE8 e3cadfa: RecordFields renders in the form-errors region only the form-level messages the banner does not already say (distinctFormMessages: deduplicated by localized message, order kept, a genuinely different message still shown). A validation problem whose only field error has pointer "" is announced once, in one role=alert region, in EN and AR. Same guard in the JourneysSection step editor; the other forms were swept (no double rendering). EN/AR component tests (16), unit test, real-stack e2e with axe; negative control.

verification.note: qa-verifier raised this finding and verified fix e3cadfa (T-DG2-FE8, frontend-ux-engineer) on candidate 45ebccc0 (source 7854770e). (1) I re-ran my unchanged round-8 spec R8-05 (charter POST body tampered with FF FE; the REAL server answers 400 validation.json at pointer "") on the qa-stack in chromium-en and chromium-ar, in both locale settings: 4/4 green. The rerun screenshots show 'The request was not valid JSON.' / 'الطلب ليس بصيغة JSON صالحة.' ONCE. In round 8 the same spec's screenshots showed it twice. (2) My new spec dg2-qa-r9.spec.ts R9-05a..e counts every role=alert region and every occurrence in the page text. The message is said exactly once (1 alert, 1 occurrence), in EN-LTR and AR-RTL, on the charter, the P1 transformation create form, the P1 admin organization create form and the ReasonDialog (archive value pool), and nothing is written (DB and API checked). The real server's other pointer-"" error (validation.unknown_field) is also said once. (3) A genuinely different second message is still shown. For this sub-check only, the browser receives a fulfilled problem: ["" validation.json, /qaNotAField validation.too_big, "" validation.json]. The banner says validation__json once, the repeated pointer-"" entry is dropped, and the form-errors list keeps exactly the distinct too_big message, once. (4) Field-pointer errors stay on their field. A server validation.blank at /outOfScope sets aria-invalid on the field and its message is in the field's aria-describedby. GateProblem, ReasonDialog, RowActions, the DefinePage activation dialog and the admin, transformation and evidence forms render ONE server banner, and pointer "" never reaches a second region (pointerToField("") is falsy; the dialogs match only their own pointer). (6) The FE8 component tests (RecordForm.alerts.test.tsx, 16 tests, including the distinct-message and field-pointer cases) pass in all 7 of my unit runs. findings.title: An unmatched route sent an application/octet-stream body answers 400 validation.content_type ('Send the request body as application/json.') instead of 404: restrictParserTo does not skip 404 requests (BE14 regression)
findings.reproduction:
Root cause. assertDeclaredMediaType skips request.is404 (apps/api/src/modules/platform/media-types.ts:82), but restrictParserTo (media-types.ts:88-100) does not. The octet-stream parser is registered with addContentTypeParser at apps/api/src/modules/evidence/routes.ts:362. For an unmatched URL, Fastify's 404 context finds that parser. consumesOf() falls back to DEFAULT_CONSUMES (application/json), and the parser calls done() with the 400 problem, so the not-found handler never runs.
Probe. zz-sec-r9-probe.test.ts S10, disposable clone at 041478cb (candidate 45ebccc0), disposable PostgreSQL 16, identical in both locale runs (probe-run1-lang-unset.log, probe-run2-lang-c-utf8.log). Requests: POST /api/v1/does-not-exist, POST /does-not-exist, and PUT and DELETE on /api/v1/transformations/{tid}/evidence (no such operations). Each was sent with and without a session.
- text/plain: 404 not_found.
- application/json {}: 404 not_found.
- application/octet-stream: 400 validation.content_type, detail 'Send the request body as application/json.'
Baseline. At the round-8 candidate cf3446e4 (probe-baseline-cf3446e4-S10-S11.log), the same octet-stream requests gave 404, so BE14 introduced this. The candidate's own test 'an unknown route keeps its 404, whatever the media type' (apps/api/test/integration/media-types.test.ts:391) sends only text/plain, so it does not catch it.
findings.expected: An unmatched route answers 404 not_found whatever the request media type, as for text/plain and JSON, and as the candidate's own test name states. The restrictParserTo wrapper should pass through when request.is404 is true, like assertDeclaredMediaType. A regression case should send application/octet-stream to an unknown route.
findings.actual: For an unknown URL, the response depends on the Content-Type. With octet-stream the client gets a 400 telling it to send JSON instead of a 404. No data is read, stored or audited. Authorization and the declared operations are unaffected: no contract operation exists for these URLs, so this is an inconsistency, not a security or integrity defect. It is Low and non-mandatory.

history.note: Raised by code-security-reviewer in DG2 round 9 while probing for remaining media-type paths after BE14. It is a BE14 regression: the same requests gave 404 at cf3446e4. Rated Low and non-mandatory because it affects only URLs with no operation, and nothing is read, stored or audited. It does not block the round.

findings.fix_summary: BE15 (WIP 08a4f63, salvaged from a run killed by a container restart) completed by BE15B e974d78: one RFC 9110 §8.3.1 media-type decision in the central preParsing hook. OWS (SP/HTAB) around ';', the essence is the lower-cased type/subtype, and parameters are tokens or quoted-strings; a malformed value, duplicate Content-Type lines, or a JSON charset other than UTF-8 is refused. An accepted header is rewritten to the canonical essence[; name=value] form before Fastify's parser lookup, so the check and the lookup cannot disagree. Every refusal, including the FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_MEDIA_TYPE backstop and restrictParserTo, names the route's declared set. An unmatched route never has its body parsed or refused: 404 not_found for every media type and framing, with Connection: close (never drained). Unit and integration tests (reviewer S10/S11 kept as regressions), a real-socket sweep, and a negative control against 3b2ab15.

verification.note:
Verified on candidate sha256:7fd1a89ca090dbdea5ae9f014853684239cbf80e89dc5cce50914155cb9d484a (source fe22d759, 544 files). I recomputed it in the working tree and in a disposable clone at HEAD 68fe3394, which adds only delivery metadata. I tested against disposable PostgreSQL 16 clusters with LANG unset (SQL_ASCII) and with LANG=C.UTF-8 (UTF8). Both runs gave identical results.
(1) My round-9 repro, zz-sec-r9-probe.test.ts S10, rerun unchanged, now PASSES in both runs. POST /api/v1/does-not-exist, POST /does-not-exist, PUT and DELETE on {T}/evidence, each sent text/plain, JSON or application/octet-stream, with and without a session: 404 every time. Round 9 gave 400 validation.content_type for octet-stream.
(2) Code. decideMediaType (media-types.ts:224-240) returns 'unmatched-route' when request.is404 is set, before any media-type check. assertDeclaredMediaType (:246-255) then deletes the Content-Type, and the preParsing hook (:296-309) sets Connection: close. I read fastify 5.6.1 to confirm the 404 path. handleRequest sees no Content-Type and calls contentTypeParser.run('') when a body is present. getParser('') matches no registered parser: only application/json and application/octet-stream are registered, and there is no catch-all. run() then hands is404 requests straight to the not-found handler (lib/contentTypeParser.js:177-181). So restrictParserTo, the round-9 root cause, can no longer be reached for an unmatched route.
(3) Adversarial probe zz-sec-r10-probe.test.ts:
- P4a (inject): 4 unmatched method/URL pairs x 7 Content-Types (HTAB, unterminated quote, */*, a latin1 charset, multipart, urlencoded, none) all gave 404 not_found with Connection: close and no error log.
- P4b (llhttp): Content-Length of 10 GB or 900 MB, Expect: 100-continue, and a chunked body that never ends all gave a prompt 404 (first byte within 3 ms), never 413 or 400, and the server closed the socket.
- P4c (llhttp keep-alive smuggling): I hid a signed-in logout in the body of an unmatched route (Content-Length, no Content-Type, chunked, and duplicate Content-Type), then pipelined a GET. The server sent exactly one response (404), then closed. GET /me still answered 200 afterwards, so the hidden request never ran.
- The rate limiter still precedes the refusal (P3b).
The candidate's own regression tests (media-types.test.ts, 'an unmatched route is 404 not_found whatever its body', 3 tests) pass in both locales.

findings.title: uploadEvidenceContent: a Content-Type that passes the essence check but that Fastify's parser lookup cannot match (e.g. 'application/octet-stream\t; x=1') is refused with a detail naming application/json, a media type the operation does not accept
findings.reproduction:
Root cause. mediaTypeEssence (apps/api/src/modules/platform/media-types.ts:63-68) trims the part before ';', so 'application/octet-stream\t; x=1' passes the central check. Fastify 5.6.1's getParser (lib/contentTypeParser.js:116-125) matches a prefix only when the next character is ';' or a space, not a tab. No parser is found, so it raises FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_MEDIA_TYPE. mapError maps that to a fixed 'Send the request body as application/json.' (apps/api/src/modules/platform/hooks.ts:66-67), whatever the route's consumes set.
Probe. zz-sec-r9-probe.test.ts S11, plus the S1 tab-before-semicolon row (Content-Length and chunked), both locale runs. POST {T}/evidence/{id}/content as the lead, with If-Match, CSRF, X-File-Name and Content-Type 'application/octet-stream\t; x=1'. Result: 400 validation.content_type, declared, nothing stored, but the detail is 'Send the request body as application/json.' For createEvidence, 'application/json\t; charset=utf-8' gives the same 400. There the detail is correct for that operation, although the essence is a declared type.
Baseline. The same at cf3446e4, so this predates BE14. BE14 made the central refusal name the route's set but left this fallback hard-coded.
findings.expected: Every media-type refusal on an operation names that operation's declared set, so here 'Send the request body as application/octet-stream.' For example, map FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_MEDIA_TYPE through undeclaredMediaTypeProblem(consumesOf(request)). Alternatively, make the essence check and the parser lookup agree on whitespace, by refusing in preParsing or by normalising.
findings.actual: A non-browser client that puts a tab before the parameters gets the declared 400, and nothing is stored or rewritten. The message tells it to switch to application/json, which this operation refuses. This affects error-message accuracy only. There is no integrity, authorization or confidentiality impact, and the web client always sends 'application/octet-stream'. It is Low and non-mandatory.

history.note: Raised by code-security-reviewer in DG2 round 9 while probing Content-Type variants after BE14. It predates BE14 (the same at cf3446e4). Rated Low and non-mandatory because the status is the declared 400, nothing is stored, and only the message text is wrong. It does not block the round.

findings.fix_summary: BE15 (WIP 08a4f63, salvaged from a run killed by a container restart) completed by BE15B e974d78: one RFC 9110 §8.3.1 media-type decision in the central preParsing hook. OWS (SP/HTAB) around ';', the essence is the lower-cased type/subtype, and parameters are tokens or quoted-strings; a malformed value, duplicate Content-Type lines, or a JSON charset other than UTF-8 is refused. An accepted header is rewritten to the canonical essence[; name=value] form before Fastify's parser lookup, so the check and the lookup cannot disagree. Every refusal, including the FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_MEDIA_TYPE backstop and restrictParserTo, names the route's declared set. An unmatched route never has its body parsed or refused: 404 not_found for every media type and framing, with Connection: close (never drained). Unit and integration tests (reviewer S10/S11 kept as regressions), a real-socket sweep, and a negative control against 3b2ab15.

verification.note:
Verified on the same candidate (sha256:7fd1a89c..., source fe22d759) in both locale runs.
(1) My round-9 repro, zz-sec-r9-probe.test.ts S11. Its assertion expected the HTAB spelling to be REFUSED with a detail naming octet-stream. It now 'fails' because the request is ACCEPTED: 'application/octet-stream\t; x=1' gives 200, stored byte-exact, with the sha256 of the raw bytes, in both framings (r9 S1 rows). This is the finding's second suggested remedy: the essence check and the parser lookup now agree. It is the genuine fix, not a regression, and that S11 assertion is obsolete.
(2) The detail half of the finding (every refusal names the operation's declared set).
- Code: mapError maps FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_MEDIA_TYPE to undeclaredMediaTypeProblem(consumesOf(request)) (hooks.ts:68-71). frameworkProblem threads the request through. decideMediaType and restrictParserTo use the same helper.
- P1: 19 spellings x 2 framings on uploadEvidenceContent. Each malformed one (OWS around '=', an empty value, no '=', an unterminated quote, a trailing backslash, a space inside type/subtype, a JSON essence, a list, a comment, NUL) gives 400 validation.content_type 'Send the request body as application/octet-stream.', declared, with nothing stored.
- P1b (llhttp, obs-text): the same detail.
- P4d (llhttp, two identical Content-Type lines; malformed): the same detail, then close.
- P6b: the FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_MEDIA_TYPE backstop names octet-stream for an octet route, and falls back to JSON without throwing when the route has no config.
(3) Agreement between the check and the lookup.
- Accepted headers are rewritten to the canonical 'essence[; name=value]' form (media-types.ts:163-165, 252) before handleRequest reads request.headers, which is raw.headers because nothing sets additionalHeaders. Only this code writes request headers (diff-scan.log).
- P6 fuzz: 20,000 random Content-Type strings over a hostile alphabet, against both declared sets. 1,760 were accepted and 38,240 refused, with 0 mismatches against fastify 5.6.1's getParser prefix rule. Every refusal names the route's set.
- P1: quoted ';', an escaped quote, a quoted ' application/json', HTAB on both sides, leading or trailing OWS, empty parameters and X="" are all stored byte-exact.
- P2: UTF-8 JSON in every legitimate spelling is created verbatim.

findings.title: A response sent before the request body is consumed leaves the connection held: an over-limit evidence upload (413 evidence.too_large) keeps its socket about 70 s after the client has gone and app.close()/SIGTERM stalls about 72 s; a refusal before the body is read (401/403/428/404) drains an unbounded body over a kept-alive connection
findings.reproduction:
Triage of the release-auditor's round-10 blocking condition 2 (docs/delivery/gates/DG2.json). Reproduced independently on the round-10 candidate sha256:7fd1a89ca090dbdea5ae9f014853684239cbf80e89dc5cce50914155cb9d484a (disposable clone at 68fe3394 = source fe22d759 + delivery metadata, candidate recomputed in the clone), Node 22.22.2, disposable PostgreSQL 16, probe docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/code-security/round-11/probes/zz-sec-r11-probe.test.ts over a real socket (llhttp), all data synthetic.
(1) R1: the Transformation Lead creates a file evidence item and POSTs 30 MiB to POST /api/v1/transformations/{T}/evidence/{id}/content (octet-stream, valid CSRF/Origin/If-Match/X-File-Name), written without waiting for backpressure, once chunked and once with Content-Length. Both: 413 evidence.too_large after 125-286 ms with Connection: keep-alive; the server never closes the socket on its own (observed 3 s); after the client destroys its socket the server still holds it and releases it only after 69,985 ms (chunked) / 69,998 ms (CL). Nothing is stored (transaction rolled back).
(2) R1c: same chunked upload, client destroys its socket 1 s after the 413, then app.close() (what src/main.ts runs on SIGTERM): 1 open connection, app.close() takes 71,994 ms.
(3) R3 (sibling): a chunked endless body to the upload route refused BEFORE the body is read - 401 (no cookie), 403 (no CSRF token), 428 (no If-Match), 404 (unknown evidence id): the refusal arrives in 25-62 ms with Connection: keep-alive, the server never closes, and the client pushes 292-302 MiB in 6 s, all read and discarded by the server. 401 needs no credentials.
Root cause (code, fe22d759): FilesystemEvidenceStore.put throws EvidenceTooLarge inside `for await (const chunk of chunks)` (apps/api/src/modules/evidence/store.ts:77-80); the async iterator's return() destroys the IncomingMessage after detaching its socket, the parser's next push() fails and it readStop()s a socket nothing reads again; the response is keep-alive, so only keepAliveTimeout (72 s) ends it and forceCloseConnections 'idle' skips it in close(). For refusals before the body is read, Node's resOnFinish calls req._dump(), which reads the whole body on a keep-alive connection; Fastify's requestTimeout 0 (apps/api/src/server.ts Fastify({...}) at fe22d759 sets none) never cuts it. Not a BE15 regression (the auditor also saw it at 041478cb).
Impact: availability only - sockets and server memory/CPU held per request, an unauthenticated client can stream an unbounded body into a kept-alive connection, and a graceful stop exceeds Compose's 10 s stop timeout (SIGKILL). No data is stored, no authorization is bypassed.
findings.expected: A response sent while the request body is not completely received closes the connection promptly (Connection: close, bounded close), never drains an unbounded body, never holds a socket after the client is gone, and app.close()/SIGTERM completes within a documented bound.
findings.actual: At 7fd1a89c: 413 with Connection: keep-alive, socket held about 70 s after the client destroyed it, app.close() 71,994 ms; refusals before the body is read keep the connection alive and drain about 300 MiB in 6 s.

history.note: raised by code-security-reviewer DG2 round 11 (triage of release-auditor round-10 blocking condition 2), reproduced at 7fd1a89c. The claimed fix (BE16 258b7e5) precedes the round-11 freeze; its verification on candidate 23e6c0a2 is in code-security-reviewer.verifications.json of the same round.

fix recorded by the orchestrator after import: fix_revision 258b7e5 (BE16), committed before the round-11 freeze (source cbdb4f6). Status unchanged: raised and verified by code-security-reviewer in round 11 (D-071).

verification.note:
Verified on candidate sha256:23e6c0a2834d2f255410e23197864ce283979964128791cfafc3e7075c7f7bad (source cbdb4f6, 547 files), recomputed in the working tree and in a disposable clone at the freeze commit 309aff2. The fix is BE16 258b7e5 (backend-workflow-engineer); I authored none of it. The same probe that reproduces the defect at 7fd1a89c was run unchanged on this candidate, on Node 22.22.2 (LANG unset) and on Node 24.21.0 (LANG=C.UTF-8), over real sockets against disposable PostgreSQL 16:
- R1 (30 MiB over-limit upload, chunked and Content-Length): 413 evidence.too_large with Connection: close; the server closes its side on its own 128-284 ms after connect; it releases the socket 479-507 ms after the client destroys it; nothing is stored. Round 10: keep-alive, never closed, released after about 70 s.
- R1c (the auditor's shutdown symptom): app.close() right after the client destroy takes 0-1 ms with 0 open connections. Round 10: 71,994 ms.
- R3 (sibling): 401/403/428/404/400/unmatched refusals of an endless chunked body: Connection: close, and the server's close (response and FIN) arrives 1-22 ms after connect. The client gets only 0.1-0.9 MiB out before the close. Round 10: keep-alive, never closed, about 300 MiB drained in 6 s.
- R2b: an over-limit body received in full (LIMIT+1, LIMIT+64 KiB) gets 413, and the same connection serves the next request (200). The connection is then released.
- No regression:
  - R2: a 2 MiB upload with invalid-UTF-8 bytes is stored with the sha256 of the raw bytes. The 200 stays keep-alive, and the same socket serves GET /me (200) and a JSON POST (201).
  - R7: bodyLimit (CL and chunked), strict UTF-8 JSON, media type (D-070), CSRF/Origin and authorization give the same status and code as at 7fd1a89c.
  - R4/R4b: unmatched routes are metered once per request in the limiter's bucket. The SPA fallback still serves index.html. Unmatched POSTs without CSRF stay 404 with no audit event. /healthz stays exempt, and every 429 carries the security headers.
  - R5 shutdown: an idle keep-alive socket is closed at once. An in-flight upload that finishes within the grace gets 200 + Connection: close and is stored byte-exact. A stalled one is cut at the grace (3,001-3,002 ms with a 3 s grace).
  - R6b/R6c/R6e: stalled headers and a stalled upload get 408 + close. An upload aborted mid-way leaves no file and no error log.
- Code:
  - connection-hygiene.ts onSend sets Connection: close only when request.raw.complete === false or while closing, and frameworkErrors applies the same. No route bypasses onSend (no hijack or raw writes in apps/api/src).
  - The destroySoon override is installed per socket, only when that close is decided. In Node 22.22.2 and 24.21.0 the only server call site is _http_server resOnFinish under res._last (checked in the built-in sources). Without destroySoon, the fallback is Node's own socket.end(). Timers are unref'd, and the cap is cleared on close.
- The candidate's own suite connection-hygiene.test.ts passes 13/13 in both locale integration runs (583/583 overall), including the SIGTERM test of src/main.ts.
Remaining in the same class, raised separately and not part of this fix: F-DG2-411 (stalled uploads hold pooled DB connections up to requestTimeout) and F-DG2-412 (an aborted JSON body logs 'unhandled error' / 500).

findings.fix_summary: BE16 258b7e5 (D-071): an onSend hook sets Connection: close on any response sent while request.raw.complete is false (frameworkErrors too), followed by a bounded lingering close (FIN, destroy after 500 ms, cap 2 s). preClose starts a 5 s shutdown grace and then closeAllConnections(), and main.ts has a backstop exit. requestTimeout 300 s is passed to http.createServer, and a client abort mid-upload gets the declared 400. Root cause: the upload's async iterator detached the socket before destroying the request, so the parser readStop()ed a socket nothing read again until keepAliveTimeout (72 s); forceCloseConnections 'idle' skipped it. Sibling: refusals before the body was read drained it via _dump() without limit. The fix preceded the round-11 freeze; code-security raised the finding from the auditor's round-10 reproduction and verified the fix in the same round (D-071).

findings.title: uploadEvidenceContent opens its database transaction before reading the body, so a few stalled uploads by one authorized user hold every pooled connection: all other users' requests and /readyz hang until requestTimeout (300 s; unbounded before BE16)
findings.reproduction:
Code (candidate 23e6c0a2, source cbdb4f6): the upload handler (apps/api/src/modules/evidence/routes.ts:417) starts db.transaction() at :421, takes the row lock (lockEvidence FOR UPDATE, :448) and only then streams the request body into the store (store.put, :464). A pooled connection stays checked out, idle in transaction, for as long as the body takes to arrive. The API pool has max 20 (apps/api/src/main.ts:25) and no checkout timeout (packages/db/src/pool.ts:42-50; statement_timeout does not apply to an idle-in-transaction session). Since BE16 the body is bounded only by requestTimeout 300 s (apps/api/src/modules/platform/connection-hygiene.ts:46); before BE16 it was unbounded.
Probe R8 (zz-sec-r11-probe.test.ts, harness pool max 5, disposable PostgreSQL 16, synthetic data): the Transformation Lead creates 6 file evidence items and opens 6 uploads over real sockets (Content-Length 10 MiB, 1 KiB sent, then nothing). 1 s later the Sponsor's GET /api/v1/me and GET /readyz get no answer within 5 s (status -1 at 5,001-5,002 ms); once the stalled sockets are destroyed /me answers 200 in 19-22 ms. Identical on 23e6c0a2 (Node 22 LANG unset; Node 24 LANG=C.UTF-8) and on 7fd1a89c. R8b on 23e6c0a2 with requestTimeoutMs 3000: the 6 uploads get 408 and /me answers 200 after about 3.1 s, i.e. the hold lasts exactly requestTimeout (default 300 s). At 7fd1a89c R8b /me is still blocked after 15 s (no request timeout there).
Attack cost: 20 sockets of about 1 KiB each, well under the 300/min rate limit, re-issued every 300 s, by any user who may upload content to an item they created (evidence.create).
findings.expected: A slow or stalled request body cannot exhaust shared database capacity: the body is received (or spooled to the store) before a pooled connection and row lock are taken, or pool checkouts and idle-in-transaction sessions are bounded so other users and /readyz keep working.
findings.actual: N stalled uploads (N = pool size, 20 in production) block every DB-backed request of every user, and /readyz, for up to 300 s per wave (indefinitely at 7fd1a89c).

history.note: raised by code-security-reviewer DG2 round 11 (class probe requested by the assignment); pre-existing at 7fd1a89c, bounded but not removed by BE16's requestTimeout.

findings.fix_summary: BE17 eb455d3: uploadEvidenceContent now runs in three phases. (1) A short transaction runs the same checks in the same order (read, exists, EDIT_OWN, file name, If-Match 428/409, archived, kind, body present/raw) and commits before any body byte is read. (2) The body is received into the store's .part (size limit 413, sha256 over the raw bytes, fsync, removed on failure) holding no connection. (3) A short write transaction re-authorises, locks the row FOR UPDATE, re-checks If-Match against the locked version (409 on a concurrent edit), inserts the content and audit, and finalises the object before commit (discarded on any failure). Sweep: no other handler awaits client I/O holding a connection or transaction (download already released). Pool defence in depth: connectionTimeoutMillis 10 s (bounded 503; /readyz not_ready), idle_in_transaction_session_timeout 30 s, a per-client error listener. Tests: R8 with pool = N (0 sessions idle in transaction; /me and /readyz prompt), stale If-Match during the body, slow-reader download, and a negative control.

verification.note:
Verified on candidate sha256:5dfecce44b9d7d4ded6ca45968c9e2686d1c011cdd7c906ba3dc9974bbdf92b8 (source 8488e7a, 552 files), recomputed in the working tree and in a clean disposable clone at the freeze commit 744af0b. The fix is BE17 eb455d3 (backend-workflow-engineer) plus the ADR-0007 §5b note be51ad7 (delivery-orchestrator); I authored none of it.
- Code: uploadEvidenceContent (apps/api/src/modules/evidence/routes.ts:443-548) has three phases.
  - Phase 1 is a short transaction with the same checks in the same order: transformation read, item 404, own-row write rule (403), file name, If-Match 428/409, archived 422, not_a_file, body present, raw byte stream. It commits before a byte of the body is read.
  - Phase 2 is store.receive into the .part temporary with no connection held. The size limit and the raw-byte sha256 are enforced while streaming, and the file is fsync'd.
  - Phase 3 is a short write transaction: openWrite (fresh ownership, transformation read, archived transformation), If-Match re-checked on the FOR UPDATE row, revision computed under the row lock, the content row, the version-guarded update, the audit event, then finalise (rename) as the last step before COMMIT. The catch discards both the final object and the .part.
  - The download route queries without a transaction and streams after the query. Worker transactions run only SQL: pg-boss send on the same tx.
- Round-11 probe re-run unchanged (sha256 0b60ece2) on Node 22.22.2 (LANG unset) and Node 24.21.0 (LANG=C.UTF-8). R8: 6 uploads stalled on a pool of 5; another user's GET /me answers 200 in 10 ms and /readyz 200 in 3-4 ms (round 11: no answer in 5 s). Its only failing assertion is R8b 'meMs > 1500', which encoded the round-11 hold; the fix inverts it (6-10 ms).
- Round-12 adversarial probe:
  - Q6b: pool max 2, 6 stalled uploads. Every api session, read as superuser, is 'idle' (none idle in transaction); /me 200 in 6-7 ms; FOR UPDATE NOWAIT on a stalled item succeeds (no row lock).
  - Q3: two uploads with the same If-Match complete together: exactly [200, 409 version_conflict], one revision, one audit event, one object on disk, and the winner's sha256 (no double revision).
  - Q2: transformation archived during the body: 422 transformation.archived, nothing stored.
  - Q4: COMMIT fails after finalise (deferred constraint): 500 at error level, no content row, no final object, no .part.
  - Q5a: client abort: no .part left.
  - Q6a: every pool session has idle_in_transaction_session_timeout 30s and statement_timeout 30s.
- The candidate's own request-io.test.ts (10/10) and packages/db pool-bounds.test.ts (7/7) pass in both locale integration runs (600/600 each).
- Pool settings break nothing: the migrate CLI uses its own pg.Client (packages/db/src/migrate.ts:129), not createPool. bootstrap and seed-dev transactions are short. The worker and the API suite pass.
- Remaining issues of a DIFFERENT class are raised separately; neither is a failure of this fix: F-DG2-440 (the phase-3 re-authorisation uses request-start grants and session; pre-existing) and F-DG2-441 (OIDC discovery inside a transaction, waiting on the IdP, not the client; pre-existing since DG1).

findings.title: A JSON request body that is aborted mid-way (client disconnect, or BE16's new requestTimeout 408) reaches the error handler as an unmapped ECONNRESET: an error-level 'unhandled error' log line and a 500 internal problem for every such request
findings.reproduction:
Probe R6 (zz-sec-r11-probe.test.ts, one fresh API instance per case, disposable PostgreSQL 16, synthetic data), candidate 23e6c0a2, identical on Node 22 (LANG unset) and Node 24 (LANG=C.UTF-8):
- R6d: POST /api/v1/transformations/{T}/evidence with valid session/CSRF, Content-Type application/json, Content-Length 100, 9 bytes sent, then the client destroys the socket: one log line level 50 msg 'unhandled error', err {message 'aborted', code ECONNRESET, statusCode 400}. Also at 7fd1a89c.
- R6a: the same stalled JSON body with requestTimeoutMs 1500: Node answers 408 and closes (correct), and the same 'unhandled error' line follows.
- Controls: R6b (stalled headers) and R6c (stalled upload) 408 with no error log; R6e (upload aborted) no error log - BE16 fixed only the upload route (abortedBodyProblem, apps/api/src/modules/evidence/routes.ts:279-283).
Cause: the JSON parser (parseAs buffer) uses Fastify's rawBody, which on a request-stream error sets err.statusCode = 400 (fastify 5.6.1 lib/contentTypeParser.js:271-273) and passes the raw Node error on. mapError (apps/api/src/modules/platform/hooks.ts:56-92) maps neither ECONNRESET/'aborted' nor a statusCode-400 error, so setErrorHandler logs 'unhandled error' (:174) and sends problems.internal() (500) to a socket that is already gone.
Impact: no client receives the 500, but any client can produce error-level log lines at will (one per aborted request, up to the rate limit), which pollutes alerting; ADR-0007 §5b treats a 500 as a failure.
findings.expected: A request whose body was not received completely is logged below error level and answered (if at all) with the declared 400 validation.malformed_request, on every body-reading route, not only uploadEvidenceContent.
findings.actual: On JSON routes it is logged as 'unhandled error' (level 50) and mapped to 500 internal.

history.note: raised by code-security-reviewer DG2 round 11 (class probe); the client-abort case is pre-existing at 7fd1a89c, the requestTimeout case is a new trigger of the same gap since BE16.

findings.fix_summary: BE17 eb455d3: central isIncompleteBodyError checked first in mapError (setErrorHandler and frameworkErrors). It matches only when request.raw.complete is false, the error has no syscall, and it is Node's request abort (ECONNRESET 'aborted', Fastify rawBody statusCode 400) or ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE on an aborted/destroyed request. The answer is the declared 400 validation.malformed_request, logged at info; the route-local abortedBodyProblem is removed. A real database ECONNRESET (read, via a resetting TCP proxy) stays a 500 with an error log. Tests: R6a (requestTimeout) and R6d (client abort) on JSON and octet-stream, plus unit over-match cases; negative control.

verification.note:
Verified on candidate sha256:5dfecce44b9d7d4ded6ca45968c9e2686d1c011cdd7c906ba3dc9974bbdf92b8 (source 8488e7a). The fix is BE17 eb455d3 (backend-workflow-engineer); I authored none of it.
- Code: isIncompleteBodyError (apps/api/src/modules/platform/hooks.ts:82-90) is checked centrally in mapError right after HttpProblem. It matches only when ALL of these hold:
  - raw.complete === false (a fully received body never matches, and inject has no such flag);
  - the error has no syscall (a database socket reset is 'read ECONNRESET' with syscall 'read');
  - either code ECONNRESET with message 'aborted' (Node's request-abort error), or ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE on a request marked aborted or destroyed.
  It answers 400 validation.malformed_request and logs at info (hooks.ts:217-219). pg protocol errors carry a SQLSTATE code; the store's EvidenceTooLarge and EvidenceStoreUnavailable carry no such code; fs errors carry a syscall. Phase-3 errors occur after the body completed (complete === true), so they never match.
- Round-11 probe re-run unchanged, on Node 22 and Node 24: R6a (stalled JSON body, requestTimeout) gets 408 with errs [] (round 11: one level-50 'unhandled error'). R6d (client aborts a JSON body) gets errs [] (round 11: 'unhandled error'). R6c and R6e (upload stalled or aborted) get errs [] with nothing stored.
- Round-12 probe:
  - Q5a: client abort mid-upload logs exactly one level-30 'request body not received completely' (code ECONNRESET), no error-level line, connection released, no .part.
  - Over-match checks: Q5b, a genuine store fault (item directory cannot be created) while the body is still incomplete, gives 503 unavailable at error level, not 400. Q4, a COMMIT failure, gives 500 internal at error level.
- The candidate's incomplete-body.test.ts (4 unit tests, including the database-ECONNRESET non-match) passes on Node 22 and 24. request-io.test.ts 'no over-match: a database-side ECONNRESET while the request body is still arriving is a 500 with an error log' passes in both locale integration runs.

findings.title: React warns 'Cannot update a component (AssignDialog) while rendering a different component (RecordDialog)': RecordForm calls onValuesChange inside a setValues updater
findings.reproduction: Disposable clone @309aff2 (candidate 23e6c0a2), `pnpm test` on Node 22 and Node 24, with LANG/LC_ALL unset and with LANG=C.UTF-8, plus one run under CPU load (7 runs). Every run prints, once, on stderr: `stderr | src/pages/team/team.test.tsx > Team (English LTR) > shows a 403 from the server in words; nothing is assigned` followed by `Cannot update a component (`AssignDialog`) while rendering a different component (`RecordDialog`). To locate the bad setState() call inside `RecordDialog`, follow the stack trace as described in https://react.dev/link/setstate-in-render`. The same line is in the round-10 unit logs (for example docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/qa/round-10/unit/node24-run1-unset.log), so it predates BE16 and is not a regression. Cause (static read): apps/web/src/components/RecordForm.tsx lines 198-203: `set` calls `props.onValuesChange?.(next)` INSIDE the `setValues((v) => ...)` updater. React may run that updater while it renders RecordDialog, so the parent's `setSelectedRole` (apps/web/src/pages/team/TeamPage.tsx line 393, the only onValuesChange user) is a state update of another component during render. Updaters must be pure; React can also call them twice (StrictMode / concurrent rendering).
findings.expected: No React warnings during the web unit tests. RecordForm reports value changes outside the state updater, for example by computing `next` from the current values and calling onValuesChange after setValues, or in an effect on `values`. The Team assign dialog's role-accountability preview keeps updating as it does today.
findings.actual: The warning appears in 7 of 7 unit runs, and in the round-10 runs. Behaviour is still correct: the test passes, the 403 is shown in words, nothing is assigned, and the role preview follows the selected role in the e2e journeys (EN and AR). The defect is the impure updater: a side effect in a React state updater, which React reports and may run twice. It is limited to the Team assign dialog today, because that is the only onValuesChange consumer.

history.note: Raised by qa-verifier in DG2 round 11 (T-DG2-REV-QA-R11) under the round-10 audit's evidence-honesty condition: every stderr line in the cited unit logs must be explained. Low, non-mandatory; pre-existing (also in round 10); not a BE16 regression; it does not affect the verdict.

findings.fix_summary: FE9 644198a: RecordForm's set() is now a pure updater, and committed values are reported to onValuesChange from an effect on values (once per new values object, never for the initial values). The sweep also made StepsEditor generate its row key outside the updater. A unit-web guard (test/react-warning-guard.ts, installed in test/setup.ts) fails any test that prints React's 'Cannot update a component ... while rendering a different component' or an act() warning; other console.error output passes through. Tests: EN/AR Team assign-dialog preview component tests, the guard's own tests, and an e2e step for the role preview; negative control.

verification.note: Verified on candidate sha256:5dfecce44b9d7d4ded6ca45968c9e2686d1c011cdd7c906ba3dc9974bbdf92b8 (552 files, source 8488e7a, freeze 744af0b). The fix is FE9 644198a by frontend-ux-engineer; qa-verifier authored none of it. (1) Unit logs: `pnpm test` ran 7 times: Node 22.22.2 x3 and Node 24.21.0 x3, alternating LANG/LC_ALL unset and LANG=C.UTF-8, plus one Node 24 run under CPU load. Every run passed 43 files / 790 tests with exit 0. `grep 'Cannot update a component'` finds 0 lines in all 7 logs, and `grep 'not wrapped in act'` and 'stderr |' blocks also find 0. In round 11 every run had one such warning. The only warning line is the known FSTDEP022 deprecation, which comes from a test-only Fastify instance in framework-errors.test.ts and also appeared in rounds 10 and 11. (2) Code: RecordForm.set now uses a pure updater, `setValues((v) => ({ ...v, [name]: value }))`. onValuesChange is called from a useEffect on `values` and skips the initial values (useRef guard). My own sweep of all 13 functional state updaters in apps/web/src found every one pure, including the StepsEditor key, which is now generated before its updater. There is no useReducer and no setState in the app. (3) Team preview, EN and AR: the product e2e step p2-17d1 passed in chromium-en and chromium-ar under both locale settings, in the product stack and the QA stack. My own UI test R12-06 cycles the Role select through KDS, TD, CM, SEC, WL, KDS and back to WL. Each time, exactly one preview is shown, and its text equals GET /role-accountabilities in the page language. The page is dir=ltr in EN and dir=rtl in AR, and the preview's computed direction matches. After Cancel, nothing is assigned and no React update warning appears. The browser console has 6 messages, all by design: the 401 from /me before sign-in, the 400 from the documented dev-login availability probe, and four 404s for GET /users/{id}, because the lead cannot read the user directory (People.tsx). Screenshots: e2e-qa-screens/{en,ar}-qa-r12-06-team-preview-sec.png. (4) The guard catches a reintroduced violation. In a throwaway clone I restored the pre-FE9 impure updater in RecordForm.set. Under both locale settings `vitest --project unit-web` then exits 1: team.test.tsx > 'shows a 403 from the server in words' fails with 'React warning printed to console.error during this test (F-DG2-430 guard ...): Cannot update a component (`AssignDialog`) while rendering a different component (`RecordDialog`)'. That gives 1 failed and 259 passed. Control C used the same violation with the guard's afterEach/afterAll removed: 8/8 pass but the warning is printed, so the guard is what fails the test. One note: React prints this warning only once per component pair per test file, so only the first offending test in a file fails. That is enough to make the suite fail.

findings.title: An in-flight evidence upload commits after the uploader's grant is revoked or their session is logged out: phase 3 'authorises again' against the request-start snapshot of grants and session, for up to requestTimeout (300 s)
findings.reproduction:
Cause: apps/api/src/modules/identity/routes.ts:120-140 (preValidation) resolves the session and loads the principal's grants ONCE per request (grants: await loadGrants(...), line 137). The policy decides on principal.grants (access/policy.ts authorize -> decide). The BE17 upload (apps/api/src/modules/evidence/routes.ts:443-548) receives the body between phase 1 and phase 3 with no time bound other than requestTimeout (DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000, platform/connection-hygiene.ts:46). Its phase-3 openWrite (routes.ts:489) re-reads ownership, the transformation's archive state and the target from the database, but re-runs the policy on the request-start grants and session.
Probe: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/code-security/round-12/probes/zz-sec-r12-probe.test.ts. Disposable clone at 744af0b (candidate 5dfecce4), disposable PostgreSQL 16, Node 22.22.2 (LANG unset) and Node 24.21.0 (LANG=C.UTF-8); identical in both runs.
- Q1: the Workstream Lead (only grant: WL at the transformation) creates a file evidence item. They start a 1 MiB upload over a real socket (If-Match, CSRF, Origin) and send 64 KiB. Their only grant is then revoked (scoped_assignment.revoked_at set; rowCount 1), and they send the rest. Result: 200, evidence_content revision 1 committed with the object on disk, evidence version 1 -> 2, review status reset, and one evidence.upload_content audit event attributed to the revoked user. A NEW request by the same session right after the revocation is refused (404: they can no longer read the transformation).
- Q1b: the Transformation Lead signs in a second session and starts an upload on it. POST /api/v1/auth/logout revokes that session (200), and GET /api/v1/me with it is then 401. The in-flight upload still completes with 200, and its content is committed.
- The same Q1/Q1b fail identically on the round-11 candidate 23e6c0a2 (clone 309aff2, before BE17; probe-r12-Q1-on-round11-23e6c0a2.log): the gap PRE-DATES BE17. BE17 did not introduce it, but its phase-3 comment ('authorization again') does not cover grants or the session, which is exactly the TOCTOU the round-12 assignment asks about.
findings.expected: A write that commits after the body was received is authorised at commit time. Phase 3 re-resolves the session (still active, not revoked or expired) and reloads the caller's grants inside the write transaction before openWrite. A grant revoked or a session logged out while the body streams is then refused (403, or 401 for the session), and the received temporary object is discarded. Equivalent: bound how long an upload may take after its authorization. Applies to every route that waits on the client between authorization and commit; today that is uploadEvidenceContent.
findings.actual: For up to requestTimeout (300 s) after a grant revocation or a logout or session revocation, an upload that was already in flight replaces the evidence item's current content and resets its review status (RESET_REVIEW). This is audited, and attributed to the user. New requests are refused correctly. Rated Medium and non-mandatory: every mutation still has a server-side authorization check, made when the request is accepted; the caller held the permission then, gains no access they did not have, and the write is audited. The defect is the revocation latency of in-flight uploads, which BE17's phase 3 claims to close but does not. The auditor may weigh the access-control aspect differently.

history.note: Raised by code-security-reviewer in DG2 round 12, while adversarially probing the BE17 three-phase upload for 'a TOCTOU between phase 1 and phase 3, a revoked grant' as the assignment directs. Pre-existing (same result at the round-11 candidate 23e6c0a2). Medium, non-mandatory (see actual). It does not block the round under the stated gate rule (no Critical, High or mandatory finding), but it should be repaired: re-resolve the session and reload grants in phase 3.

findings.fix_summary: BE18A 8c0083e: before the change, the upload's phase-3 write transaction re-authorises against fresh state through the identity module's own resolution: the session must still be active (not revoked, logged out, idle- or absolute-expired, user not disabled; else 401 and the session-ended problem), and the caller's grants are reloaded and the policy re-run (403 with the denied-mutation audit). The received object is discarded on refusal. Sweep: uploadEvidenceContent is the only route that waits on the client between preValidation and its commit. Residual window: the few ms of phase 3's own transaction. Tests Q1 (grant revoked mid-body: 403, nothing committed), Q1b (logout: 401), idle and absolute expiry, disabled user, a re-grant control; negative control on 8c02475.

verification.note:
Verified on candidate sha256:6824b8b8d36a688178a058c11c4882737a79cf7f39b438dcf2390eafb88d3afc (source aa0a68f, 556 files), recomputed in the working tree and in a clean disposable clone at the freeze commit 5699f72. The fix is BE18A 8c0083e (backend-workflow-engineer) plus D-073 (delivery-orchestrator); I authored none of it.
- Code:
  - Phase 3 of uploadEvidenceContent (apps/api/src/modules/evidence/routes.ts:514-571) calls openWrite(..., { atCommit: true }) inside its write transaction.
  - openWrite (transformations/register-kit.ts:262-269) then calls refreshPrincipal (access/request.ts:42-50), which runs request.reauthenticate(tx). That is the identity module's own principalFor (identity/routes.ts:124-140), the same function the preValidation hook uses. It runs resolveSession on the tx (token hash, revoked_at null, idle and absolute expiry vs now(), user status active, identity/sessions.ts:75-94), checks the same user id and reloads the grants with loadGrants(tx).
  - A null result is 401 unauthenticated. The read and write gates then run on the RELOADED principal, and a 404 from the read gate becomes 403 forbidden with the denial kept (commitTimeDenial), so denials.ts audits authorization.denied.
  - The catch at routes.ts:572-575 discards the temporary and the final object on every refusal. It fails closed: a request without a resolver gets 401.
  - JSON routes are not exposed: Fastify parses the whole body BEFORE preValidation, so their request-start snapshot is taken after the client has finished sending. The upload is the only route whose parser passes the raw stream (evidence/routes.ts:388-391; the other parser is JSON, server.ts:207-210).
- My round-12 reproductions, re-run UNCHANGED (zz-sec-r12-probe sha 71cbe705) on Node 22.22.2 (LANG unset) and Node 24.21.0 (LANG=C.UTF-8):
  - Q1 (grant revoked while the body streams) is now 403 forbidden with nothing stored, no .part and no upload audit (round 12: 200).
  - Q1b (session logged out while the body streams) is now 401 unauthenticated with nothing stored (round 12: 200).
  - Q2-Q6b are unchanged (9/9 pass).
- New adversarial probe zz-sec-r13-probe (sha 8ae4840f), on both Node versions:
  - S1: a role DOWNGRADE (WL -> AUD at the same scope, read kept, evidence.create lost) while the body streams gives 403, one authorization.denied audit '... requires evidence.create', and nothing stored.
  - S2: the item's owner reassigned away from the uploader while the body streams gives 403, nothing stored.
- The candidate's commit-time-auth.test.ts (8/8) passes in both locale integration runs. It covers revocation, logout, idle and absolute expiry, a disabled user, a positive control and re-grant (the current grants win).
- Residual (measured, S3; NOT a finding):
  - The authority is read at the start of phase 3, and the item's FOR UPDATE lock is taken after it. A revocation that commits while phase 3 waits for that lock does not stop the commit (200).
  - This is the stated residual window (phase 3's own transaction). Only a concurrent transaction holding the item's row lock can lengthen it, and since BE17 none waits on a client. statement_timeout (30 s) bounds it, and the uploader cannot extend it through the API.
  - Suggested hardening, optional: take the row lock before re-authorising.

findings.title: OIDC discovery (a remote call to the IdP) runs inside an open database transaction in GET /api/v1/auth/login: while the IdP is slow or unreachable, unauthenticated login attempts hold pooled connections 'idle in transaction' for the 10 s discovery timeout and stall signed-in users
findings.reproduction:
apps/api/src/modules/identity/routes.ts:268 runs db.transaction().execute((tx) => oidc.startLogin(tx, ...)). Kysely checks out a connection and issues BEGIN before the callback. startLogin (apps/api/src/modules/identity/oidc.ts:58-59) first awaits this.configuration_() (oidc.ts:37-50), which performs OIDC discovery over HTTP with a 10 s default timeout. The result is cached only on success; a failure clears the cache, so every login retries discovery while the IdP is down. This contradicts the BE17 sweep note in packages/db/src/pool.ts:34 ('No application transaction waits on anything but the database (no client I/O, no remote call)').
Probe: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/code-security/round-12/probes/zz-sec-r12-oidc-probe.test.ts. Disposable clone at 744af0b (candidate 5dfecce4), disposable PostgreSQL 16, Node 22.22.2 and 24.21.0, identical results. The IdP is a local TCP server that accepts and never answers. OidcService uses its default discovery timeout (10 s), AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE is the product default (20), and the pool max is 3. Three unauthenticated GET /api/v1/auth/login run concurrently. After 1 s, pg_stat_activity read as superuser shows 3 api sessions 'idle in transaction'. A signed-in Sponsor's GET /api/v1/me then takes 9,010-9,029 ms. The logins end at 10.0 s with 302 /login?error=idp_unavailable. With the production pool (max 10) and 20 logins per minute per IP, a login storm during an IdP outage (users retrying) can exhaust the pool. Signed-in users then get the bounded 503 after connectionTimeoutMillis (10 s) instead of being served. Pre-existing since DG1 (8332624).
findings.expected: No transaction is open while waiting on the IdP: resolve the OIDC configuration (discovery) before db.transaction(), then insert the login state in a short transaction. The OIDC callback already does this (consumeState in its own transaction, then the token exchange outside any transaction, routes.ts:302-347).
findings.actual: Each login attempt holds a pooled connection, and an open transaction, for up to the discovery timeout whenever discovery is not cached. Rated Low and non-mandatory: it needs an IdP outage or slowness, is bounded at 10 s per attempt and rate-limited per IP, needs no credentials, has no confidentiality or integrity impact, and with BE17's connectionTimeoutMillis it degrades to a declared 503 rather than a hang.

history.note: Raised by code-security-reviewer in DG2 round 12, during the assigned sweep for 'any remaining path that holds a pooled connection, transaction or row lock while it waits'. This one waits on the IdP rather than the HTTP client. Pre-existing since DG1. Low, non-mandatory; it does not block the round.

findings.fix_summary: BE18A 8c0083e: GET /auth/login resolves the OIDC configuration (discovery) via prepareLogin before any transaction, then saveLoginState inserts the state in a short transaction. Discovery failure is still 302 /login?error=idp_unavailable. A class sweep of every non-database await inside a db.transaction callback or a checked-out client (API, worker, packages) found and fixed this one; the evidence finalise rename is the documented exception. The pool.ts sweep note is corrected. Test Q7: a never-answering IdP with pool max 3 leaves no session idle in transaction, and /me stays prompt; negative control.

verification.note:
Verified on candidate sha256:6824b8b8d36a688178a058c11c4882737a79cf7f39b438dcf2390eafb88d3afc (source aa0a68f). The fix is BE18A 8c0083e (backend-workflow-engineer); I authored none of it.
- Code:
  - GET /api/v1/auth/login (identity/routes.ts:290-296) now calls oidc.prepareLogin first, outside any transaction (identity/oidc.ts:71-88). That covers OIDC discovery via configuration_(), the random state, nonce and PKCE verifier, and the authorization URL. Only then does it run saveLoginState in a short transaction that does nothing but INSERT INTO oidc_login_state.
  - The state is still stored as sha256 with the nonce, PKCE verifier, return_to and sha256(browser binding), and the 10-minute expiry is unchanged. The login cookie is still set only after the insert succeeded.
  - The callback is unchanged. consumeState (its own transaction), exchange (remote, outside any transaction) and resolveOidcUser (its own transaction) run one after another. endSessionUrl runs after the logout transaction.
- My round-12 reproduction, re-run UNCHANGED (zz-sec-r12-oidc-probe sha db10609c) on Node 22 and Node 24, with a never-answering IdP, pool max 3 and three concurrent logins:
  - all three API sessions are 'idle' (round 12: 'idle in transaction');
  - a signed-in user's /me answers 200 in 18-22 ms (round 12: 9.0 s);
