  The candidate's commit-time-auth.test.ts Q7 and oidc.test.ts (33/33: state, nonce, PKCE, browser binding) pass in both locale runs.
- Independent sweep:
  - I wrote my own TypeScript-AST scan (await-sweep.mjs, 135 files across apps/*/src and packages/*/src) of every await in a transaction callback, in a function taking a Tx, DbOrTx, Transaction or client, and in pooled-client checkouts.
  - It found no remote or slow non-database await inside a transaction. The only one is the documented store.finalise (a local atomic rename) as the last step before COMMIT.
  - The worker's pg-boss send runs on the same transaction. The rest are Kysely builders, closures over tx, the /readyz checkout and the operator CLI.

findings.title: Regression (BE17): an evidence upload in flight at SIGTERM leaves an orphaned .part file with the partial upload bytes in the evidence store, and it is never removed
findings.reproduction: Disposable clone at 744af0b (candidate 5dfecce4, source 8488e7a), `pnpm -r build`, e2e/support/qa-stack.sh (real API apps/api/dist/main.js + disposable PostgreSQL 16 + filesystem evidence store). Probe R12-07 in docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/qa/tests/round-12/e2e/dg2-qa-r12.spec.ts: (1) start a separate API process from the same build. (2) As the item's owner, POST /transformations/{t}/evidence/{e}/content with Content-Length 10 MiB and If-Match, send 2 MiB, then stall with the client socket left open. The store now holds <org>/<t>/<e>/<content>.part (2,097,152 B). (3) Send SIGTERM to the API. main.ts runs app.close(), the 5 s grace expires, the connection is destroyed, and the process exits 0 in about 5.02 s. (4) List the store. The same failure also shows in qa-verifier's round-11 regression test R11-02(b) ('stored files 1'), which fails in chromium-en and chromium-ar under both locale settings (4 of 4 runs). The probe was run in both projects and both locale settings with the same result. Control 1, same build: the same stall, but the CLIENT aborts while the process keeps running, leaves nothing (the .part is removed). Control 2, the round-11 freeze 309aff2 (pre-BE17): the identical probe leaves nothing after SIGTERM, and R11-02(b) passed there in 4 of 4 runs. Probable cause (static read): BE17 moved the body into phase 2, store.receive(), which holds no pooled connection. receive() removes its temporary only in its catch block, after the request stream errors, and that cleanup is asynchronous (handle.close, then rm). main.ts calls `await app.close(); await db.destroy(); process.exit(0)`. Before BE17 the in-flight upload held a checked-out pool client, so db.destroy() waited until the handler had cleaned up and rolled back. Now db.destroy() resolves at once and process.exit(0) runs before rm(temp). Nothing else removes a .part file: there is no startup sweep and no worker job, and retention deletes are P6.
findings.expected: A failed upload stores nothing, which is the BE17 contract ('Any failure after phase 2 started discards the temporary and the final object') and was the behaviour before BE17. That includes an upload cut by a graceful shutdown: SIGTERM with an upload in flight leaves no final object and no .part file. For example, shutdown could wait, within the grace or backstop, for in-flight upload handlers to finish their cleanup before process.exit. Or the store could sweep stale .part objects at start-up.
findings.actual: After SIGTERM the store keeps <org>/<t>/<e>/<uuid>.part (2,097,152 B of the user's partial upload) with no evidence_content row. It is not downloadable (GET content returns 404, currentContentId is null). It is still there after a new API process starts on the same store. Every rolling restart or deploy with an upload in flight leaks up to 25 MiB of user-supplied evidence bytes per upload. Nothing reports, governs or deletes them. Record integrity is intact: no committed row points at a missing or partial object, and the bytes are never served. That is why this is Medium and not mandatory. The leftover is an unbounded storage leak and uncontrolled retention of partial evidence content, a regression from round 11.

history.note: Raised by qa-verifier in DG2 round 12 (T-DG2-REV-QA-R12). The full regression's R11-02(b) failed 4 of 4 runs. The dedicated probe R12-07 identifies the leftover .part and shows it survives a restart. The same probe on the round-11 freeze 309aff2 leaves nothing, so this is a BE17 regression. Medium, non-mandatory. Because it is a regression, the round-12 qa verdict is FAIL.

findings.fix_summary: BE18A 8c0083e: an in-flight tracker (platform/in-flight.ts) lets graceful shutdown wait, bounded at 3 s and within the backstop, for every handler to settle, including its catch/finally cleanup, before db.destroy() and process.exit. The filesystem evidence store sweeps .part temporaries older than a safe age (1 h, beyond requestTimeout plus grace, across instances) at start-up, logged at info; final objects are never touched. Tests: R12-07 (stalled upload then SIGTERM: no .part, no final object, exit 0), an actively streaming upload, and the sweep keeping fresh temporaries and final objects; qa's R11-02 and R12-07 specs pass byte-identical; negative control on 8c02475.

verification.note: Verified on candidate sha256:6824b8b8d36a688178a058c11c4882737a79cf7f39b438dcf2390eafb88d3afc (556 files, source aa0a68f1, freeze 5699f72). The fix is BE18A 8c0083e (D-073) by backend-workflow-engineer; qa-verifier authored none of it. All runs used the real built API (apps/api/dist/main.js), a disposable PostgreSQL 16 (UTF8, C) and the filesystem evidence store, through e2e/support/qa-stack.sh, with --workers=1. Each spec ran in chromium-en and chromium-ar, once with LANG/LC_ALL unset and once with LANG=C.UTF-8. (1) My original reproductions now pass in all 4 runs per test. R12-07: an upload stalled in flight at SIGTERM exits 0 in about 5.02-5.04 s; the store held a 2,097,152 B .part during the stall and holds nothing after exit; no content row, currentContentId null, GET content 404. The client-abort control also leaves nothing. R11-02(b): stored files 0 and exit 0. (2) New R13-01: two uploads were ACTIVELY STREAMING through the whole 5 s grace (about 6.7 MB of a declared 24 MiB sent when the server cut them) and a third was stalled. SIGTERM exits 0 in 5,023-5,045 ms, inside the 10 s backstop. The server closed all 3 sockets, 'shut down' is logged, there is no settle-period warning and no error-level line. Nothing is left in the store after exit or after a restart on the same store; 0 content rows and versions unchanged. (3) New R13-02 drain check: an upload that finishes inside the grace still commits (200), byte-exact with sha256 = DB, leaves only its final object (no .part) and exits 0. (4) New R13-03 start-up sweep on a new API process over the shared store. Exactly the stale <uuid>.part (mtime 2 h ago, 4,096 B) is removed. It is logged at info as 'evidence store: stale temporary object removed' with the root-relative key (no absolute path), sizeBytes 4096 and ageMs about 7.2e6. The finished line reports removed 1 and keptFresh equal to the number of fresh temporaries actually present, with olderThanMs 3600000. All of these are kept: a fresh .part, a 50-minute-old .part, a 3-hour-old FINAL object, a real committed object back-dated to 2 h (still downloadable byte-exact), a stale 'notes.part', an upper-case-UUID .part, stale .part files at depth 2 and depth 4, a stale '<uuid>.part' DIRECTORY, a directory symlink to an outside tree holding a stale .part, and a '<uuid>.part' symlink to an outside stale file. The sha256 of every other object in the store is unchanged. (5) Negative control: the same R13-01 and R13-03 on the round-12 freeze 744af0b (pre-BE18A) fail in both projects, as expected. After SIGTERM, .part files of 6,782,976 B, 6,782,976 B and 1,048,576 B remain, and no sweep runs (no finished line, nothing removed). So the probes detect the defect. (6) Static reading agrees with this: main.ts runs app.close(), then inFlight.settled(3 000 ms), then db.destroy(), then process.exit(0). Every route registered after registerInFlightTracking is tracked, and so are the failed-mutation audit and the sweep. During my development of R13-03, the first run failed because my own snapshot followed a symlink; the product's sweep was correct. That is explained in 18-r13-spec-dev-run1.log and the record.

findings.title: When a session ends while the app is open (access revoked, signed out elsewhere, expiry, or the D-073 commit-time refusal of an upload), the web client loops forever between /login?error=session_expired and the page: blank screen, no sign-in form, no localized message, about 130-140 /me requests per second; with default rate limits it locks the IP out and shows a stale signed-in shell
findings.reproduction:
Disposable clone at 5699f721 (candidate 6824b8b8…, source aa0a68f1). Fresh PostgreSQL 16 and API (AUTH_MODE=dev, synthetic seed, apps/web/dist served), Chromium, Node 24.21.0.
(1) Generic case, `with-stack.sh node rv/r13-session-end-ui.mjs`: dev.lead signs in through the form and is on My work. The session is ended from outside the page (POST /api/v1/auth/logout with the browser's own cookie, i.e. 'signed out in another tab'). The user clicks the in-app link to /transformations. Sampled every 250 ms for 10 s, the URL alternates /transformations <-> /login?returnTo=…&error=session_expired 18 (EN) and 21 (AR) times. The page is blank (no text, no input) the whole time, the localized 'Your session ended…' / 'انتهت جلستك…' message never appears, and the tab sends 1411 (EN) and 1265 (AR) /me requests in 10 s. Control: the same session end followed by a page reload lands on the sign-in form in about 0.4 s with 2 /me requests.
(2) The D-073 case, `r13-ui.mjs` (c) and `r13-ui-withdrawn.mjs`: dev.nobody holds TL on a transformation and opens the evidence Upload dialog. An administrator revokes the assignment through POST /api/v1/role-assignments/{id}/revoke, which also ends the sessions. The user confirms the upload: the API answers 401 unauthenticated, correctly, and nothing is stored. The dialog shows the localized message for a few ms, then the page enters the same blank loop: 15 s of alternation and thousands of /me 401s.
(3) Default rate limits (RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=300, `with-stack-default-limits.sh node rv/r13-session-end-ui.mjs`): after about 283 /me calls in about 1.8 s the client-IP bucket is exhausted, because an ended session's cookie is keyed by IP. The page then shows the signed-out user the app shell with their stale name, 'Sign out' and 'Something went wrong / Too many requests', not the sign-in form. The next browser context from the same IP could not get a sign-in form at all (locator timeout).
Cause, by reading the code: apps/web/src/auth/session.tsx RequireSession redirects to /login?…&error=session_expired when /me answers 401 while me.data (the last successful /me) is still cached. apps/web/src/pages/LoginPage.tsx line 66 `if (me.data) return <Navigate to={returnTo} replace />` sees that same stale cached me.data and sends the user straight back, and each mount re-probes /me. The code is unchanged since DG1 (4cd9224) and the web was not touched by D-073. The defect is pre-existing, but D-073's new commit-time 401 on uploads now leads into it too.
findings.expected: When a request answers 401 because the session ended (revocation, sign-out elsewhere, idle or absolute expiry, or the D-073 commit-time re-authorisation), the user lands once on the sign-in page. It shows the localized session-ended message (auth.errors.session_expired, EN LTR / AR RTL) and the sign-in form, with a bounded number of /me requests. Signing in again returns them to their page. The cached identity is cleared, so a signed-out user never sees a stale signed-in shell, and one stuck tab never exhausts the rate-limit bucket of everyone behind the same IP.
findings.actual: The user is stuck on a blank page that alternates between /login and the original route indefinitely, until they manually reload. There is no message and no form. The tab sends about 130-140 /me requests per second. With the product's default limits this exhausts the shared per-IP bucket in about 2 s. The tab then shows a stale signed-in shell with 'Too many requests', and other sign-ins from that IP are refused for the rest of the minute. The server side behaves correctly throughout: 401 unauthenticated, nothing stored, no temporary file left. Only the client's session-end handling is broken.

history.note: Raised by domain-reviewer in DG2 round 13 (T-DG2-REV-DOM-R13) while confirming the D-073 user outcomes ('an upload is refused if access is withdrawn or the user signs out' and 'sign-in still works'). Reproduced in EN and AR, with and without the D-073 upload path, and with the product's default rate limits. Pre-existing since DG1 (4cd9224) in the web client; the D-073 server behaviour itself is correct. High: the re-authentication workflow after a session ends is broken for every screen, and with default limits one stuck tab locks its IP out. Not marked mandatory: no access-control, data-integrity or calculation breach (the server refuses correctly).

findings.fix_summary: FE10 8cb3bb8: one session-end rule in the web API client (module phase unknown/active/ended). Any request (including /me, a page query, a mutation or the upload dialog) that answers 401 unauthenticated while the phase is active ends the session exactly once and drops the CSRF token. A 403, another 401 code, or a 401 with no active session is not a session end. RequireSession then renders nothing (no stale shell), disables its /me query, clears the cached identity and every session-scoped query once, and navigates once to /login?returnTo=...&error=session_expired. LoginPage decides 'already signed in' only from a fresh /me (refetchOnMount always, dataUpdatedAt >= mount). Signing out in this tab is not a session end. At most 2 /me per session end. Tests: session-end.test.tsx (EN/AR, every trigger, bounded /me, 403 not an end) and e2e session-end.spec.ts (sign-out elsewhere and an in-app link, the commit-time upload refusal, product default rate limits with a second context from the same IP signing in, axe 0); negative control on HEAD.

verification.note:
Verified on candidate sha256:9f3ca298 (source ea9051b2, FE10 8cb3bb8), in EN (LTR) and AR (RTL), in a disposable stack with synthetic data.
- My round-13 reproductions now pass unchanged. r13-session-end-ui: in-app link and reload, 4/4, with raised and default limits; each in-app link makes 1 /me where round 13 made about 130 per second. r13-ui (c): after the 401 upload refusal the user is on /login with the localized message, with no EN leak and 0 revisions. r13-ui-withdrawn: the message on /login at about 270 ms, and signing in again returns to the evidence page.
- New r14-session-end-ui, 31/31 with raised limits and 31/31 with the product's default limits. It covers a real second tab clicking Sign out, an administrator revocation, idle expiry, absolute expiry and logout by API. Every trigger lands exactly once on /login?returnTo=/transformations&error=session_expired, with the form and the localized message and the correct dir. Each makes /me = 1 in 10 s, with 0 429s and no stale shell. A second context from the same IP signs in, and signing in again returns to /transformations.
- Source: the session phase lives in the API client (unknown/active/ended). A 401 'unauthenticated' while active ends the session once, and a 403 never does. RequireSession disables /me, clears the cache once and navigates once. LoginPage trusts only a /me answered after it mounted.
- Limit noted, not a defect: a tab learns that its session ended only from its next server request. A navigation served entirely from cache shows the page until then.

findings.title: A session that ends while the sign-in page is shown never clears the session-scoped query cache: the next identity to sign in in that tab (development form, or a /me re-probe after an IdP sign-in in another tab) is shown the previous user's cached records
findings.reproduction:
FE10 moved the session-end rule into the API client (apps/web/src/api/client.ts:99 endSession: a 401 `unauthenticated` while the phase is "active" makes it "ended"). The cache is cleared only by <RequireSession> (apps/web/src/auth/session.tsx:52-58: claimSessionEnd() then queryClient.removeQueries()), so only when that component is mounted, or mounts later while the phase is still "ended". The sign-in page is outside <RequireSession> (apps/web/src/app/router.tsx:38). It re-probes /me on mount (apps/web/src/pages/LoginPage.tsx:60, refetchOnMount "always") through the same client, so a 401 there ends the session but clears nothing. The next successful GET /me then sets the phase back to "active" (apps/web/src/api/queries.ts:62 markSessionActive), the end is never claimed, and the sign-in page navigates to returnTo (LoginPage.tsx:70) with the previous user's queries still cached.
The precondition is the sign-in page being shown in the same document while the phase is "active". That happens when the browser Back button returns to an in-document /login history entry, for example one pushed by the sign-in page's own wordmark link (LoginPage.tsx:80), after the user signed in in that document (development form, or a refocus /me re-probe after an IdP sign-in in another tab).
Probe: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/code-security/round-14/probes/zz-sec-r14-web-probe.test.tsx (sha256 2b64ba54), copied into a disposable clone of candidate 9f3ca298 (d99de98), unit-web project, jsdom, the product's own fixtures, SYNTHETIC data. Identical on Node 22.22.2 and Node 24.21.0 (probe-web-node22.log, probe-web-node24.log).
W5 (development sign-in): user A is on /transformations and sees TR-A-SECRET. A's session ends, and the tab goes Back to /login?returnTo=%2Ftransformations: GET /me 401, phase "ended", and 1 transformations query is still cached. User B signs in with the development form (POST /auth/dev-login 204, GET /me 200 as "Synthetic User B"). The app navigates to /transformations, and with B's list request still in flight the page shows B's name and A's row TR-A-SECRET.
W5b (OIDC mode, development sign-in 404): same, but B signs in at the IdP in another tab and this tab's /me is re-probed (as refetchOnWindowFocus does in production). Same result: B sees TR-A-SECRET.
Control: when the session ends while <RequireSession> is mounted (the product's own session-end.test.tsx, and W6 here), the cache is cleared and nothing leaks.
findings.expected: When a session ends, whatever page is shown, the cached identity and every session-scoped query are removed before any later identity can render. A user who signs in afterwards in the same tab never sees records fetched under the previous session.
findings.actual: The cache is cleared only if <RequireSession> observes the "ended" phase. A session that ends on the sign-in page is never claimed. The next sign-in in that tab renders the previous user's cached records (TR-A-SECRET) under the new user's identity, until the new user's own requests replace them. Server-side authorisation is intact: no API response ever carries A's data to B; the exposure is data A already held in that tab's memory. Rated Medium, not mandatory, for that reason and the narrow preconditions. Suggested fix: clear the session-scoped cache where the phase changes, independent of which route is mounted (for example a phase subscriber in AppProviders that removes every query when the phase becomes "ended"), or remove every query on any transition into "active" whose user differs from the cached one.

findings.reproduction:
FE13 (29da00d) removes every session-scoped query when GET /me returns another identity (api/queries.ts fetchMe -> noteSessionIdentity -> app/App.tsx resetSessionCache: cancelQueries, removeQueries, getMutationCache().clear()). Its comment says an answer fetched under the previous session 'cannot land in the cache afterwards'. That holds for queries but not for the success continuations of in-flight writes. Those are plain async handlers that call queryClient.setQueryData after `await api.send(...)`: TransformationEditPage.tsx:130 (and the conflict path :140), TransformationDetailPage.tsx:143 (archive), OrganizationsPage.tsx:255/572 and UsersPage.tsx:387. They are not TanStack mutations, so clearing the mutation cache does not stop them. The handler of the unmounted A subtree still holds the QueryClient and the router.
Probe: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/code-security/round-15/probes/zz-sec-r15-web-probe.test.tsx case X3 (sha256 bd97dbc9), unit-web, jsdom, the product's own fixtures, SYNTHETIC data, in a disposable clone of candidate 3f01c610 (9236a9f). The PATCH is sent with A's cookie and its answer is held. In another tab A signs out and B (another user id and session) signs in; this tab re-probes /me (refocus) and gets B. FE13 resets the cache and remounts the subtree, and the header shows 'Synthetic User B'. A's PATCH is then answered 200. The edit page's handler calls setQueryData(['transformation', id], A's record) and navigates to /transformations/{id}. Result: path /transformations/{id}, header B, cache name = A-PATCHED-SECRET, and B sees A-PATCHED-SECRET. After B's own GET of that record answers 404 (B has no access), B still sees it and the cache still holds it. findings.expected: No response to a request issued under a previous identity (session) is written into the cache or rendered once this tab has moved to another identity. Possible fix: give each identity a generation counter in the API client. apiRequest records it when the request is sent; if the identity changed or the session ended before the answer arrives, it throws a 'session changed' error instead of returning data. That covers every setQueryData path at once, without per-page guards. Alternatively, guard each success handler.
findings.actual: A's freshly edited record is written into the new identity's cache and shown to B, who is navigated to it. It stays on screen after B's own refetch fails with 404. Server-side authorisation is intact: no API response ever carries A's data to B, and the exposure is a record A had just edited in that tab. The exposure needs a narrow race. A write has to stay in flight while A signs out and B signs in in another tab of the same browser profile, and this tab has to re-probe /me before the write is answered (slow server or network). For that reason it is rated Low and not mandatory. It is the same class as F-DG2-500 but a different mechanism (a late write rather than an uncleared cache), and FE13's defence in depth already covers it when the session ended in this tab (X3b).

findings.title: The formula engine's 'no dynamic code' guards (ESLint override and the fuzz.test.ts source scan) both accept code that builds and runs a function from a string
findings.reproduction: In a disposable clone at ec45ef1, append to packages/shared/src/formula/evaluate.ts: `import { createRequire } from "node:module"`; `Reflect.construct(Function, ["return 1"])`; `Reflect.apply(Function, null, ["return 1"])`; `createRequire(import.meta.url)("vm")`; `Object.getPrototypeOf(function* () {})["constructor"]("yield 1")`; `const __F = Function; __F("return 1")`. Run `npx eslint packages/shared/src/formula/evaluate.ts` and `pnpm vitest run --project unit-node packages/shared/src/formula/fuzz.test.ts -t "source scan"`. In Node, `const F = Function; F("return 6*7")()` returns 42, so these forms do run code. The override at eslint.config.js:37-84 lists only no-eval, no-implied-eval, no-new-func, vm/node:vm import paths, ImportExpression, WithStatement, plain or member timer calls and non-computed `.constructor(...)` calls. The scan at packages/shared/src/formula/fuzz.test.ts:214-240 matches `eval(`, `new Function`, `Function(`, vm `from`/`require(`, `import(`, `with(`, timers and `globalThis`. A separate file with the same bypasses passes lint the same way: the five named forms are refused and the six bypasses are not.
findings.expected: ADR-0024 §6 says the ESLint override 'enforces' that nothing under packages/shared/src/formula evaluates text as code, and that the source scan backs it up. Any reference to the Function constructor (direct, aliased, through Reflect.construct or Reflect.apply, or as a computed ['constructor'] member) and any module loading other than static imports (createRequire, require) should fail lint or the scan. Examples: no-restricted-globals for Function, eval and Reflect; no-restricted-syntax for Identifier[name='Function'], computed MemberExpression 'constructor' and createRequire/require calls; the same patterns added to the scan.
findings.actual: eslint exits 0 and the source-scan test passes (1 passed, 4 skipped by -t) with all five bypass forms present in evaluate.ts. The shipped engine itself contains no dynamic code path: the S6 scan found none and probe C ran 20,000 fuzz strings plus injection strings and evaluated nothing outside the grammar. The defect is that the guard does not hold against these forms if one is introduced later. The engine's actual security is not affected.

history.note: Raised by code-security-reviewer in DG3 round 1 (session afa637ec). Low and non-mandatory: the guard has a coverage gap, and the shipped engine has no dynamic code. It does not block the gate verdict.

findings.fix_summary: T-DG3-KBE-F 0fb892c (third pass, after the round-3 verification FAILED): every catch in the engine's import closure (validateFormula, evaluateFormula, evaluateAst, value.ts formatDecimal) rethrows EvalError, so an exercised code-generating path fails every no-codegen test that reaches it; independently, every fuzz.test.ts outcome check and every formula.test.ts rejection row refuses params.reason 'internal'; regression tests in the no-codegen project. value.ts gets the engine-source lint block with a decimal.js-only allowlist and joins the scan; engineImportClosure() pins the transitive closure (six formula sources + value.ts, decimal.js only) to the guarded set, with a lint-coverage test (unit-node). Reviewer probes: S1 and S3 now refused at run time, V1 by lint+scan, V2 by all three; the 18 earlier forms stay refused. ADR-0024 §6 corrected. Production behaviour for non-EvalError internal errors unchanged (422 formula.syntax 'internal'); integration 793/793.

verification.note:
Not closed on candidate sha256:8376d762… (source 171a0b57). Severity stays Low and non-mandatory: the shipped engine generates no code, lints clean, and its results are unchanged (probe C, 3,000-tree exact oracle, Node 22 and 24, both unit projects). The open defect is in the guard's stated guarantee (ADR-0024 §6), as in round 3.

WHAT THE REPAIR CLOSES (verified, disposable clones at 171a0b57, Node 22):
- Round-3 reason (1), the engine's catch-all swallowing an exercised EvalError, is fixed. My round-3 guard-layers-probe.mjs, run verbatim (sha256 7887455b…):
  - S1 is refused at run time (3 flag-only failures, including 'rejects "été" … offset 0' and two fuzz tests).
  - S2: 8 flag-only failures.
  - S3: 2 flag-only failures.
  - In round 3, S1 and S3 passed all three layers.
- My round-3 exercised-probe.mjs, run verbatim: fuzz.test.ts's own three fuzz tests now fail with 'EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed', and vitest exits 1. The probe's own S1/S3 tests fail BY DESIGN: they assert the round-3 swallow, which no longer happens.
- Round-3 reason (2), ../value.ts being unguarded, is fixed:
  - V1 (node:vm in value.ts) is refused by lint ('decimal.js only' allowlist) and by the scan.
  - V2 (new Function in value.ts) is refused by lint, the scan and the run-time layer (61 flag-only failures).
- The 18 earlier forms (round-2 guard-bypass-probe.mjs, verbatim): O1–O6 and N1–N12 are all eslint=1 and scan=1.
- Every catch in the 7-file closure rethrows EvalError. There are five catch clauses: the four named in the ADR, plus parse.ts, which rethrows anything that is not its own ParseFailure. decimal.js 10.6.0 has no try/catch, eval( or Function(.
- An EvalError wrapped with `cause` is refused at run time through the internal-failure rule (swallow-probe W5 and W6: 3 and 2 flag-only failures). An unhandled async rejection is refused (W3: 7,656 unhandled EvalErrors, exit 1).
- Every outcome check in fuzz.test.ts and every rejection-table row refuses reason 'internal' (read in source).
- The closure test follows import, export-from, `export *` and type-only forms. It misses a string-named specifier (`export { "x" as y } from "../scoring.ts"`), but ESLint refuses that module (closure-parser-probe.log X1), so layer 1 holds.
- API: an EvalError from the engine is a generic 500 `internal` with no detail, and nothing is written (sec-r4-evalerror-api-v2, both environments). No other API status changed: integration 793/793 twice.

WHY IT IS NOT CLOSED. ADR-0024 §6 layer 3 states: 'Guarantee. Any engine path that generates code from a string fails the engine's tests, provided a test exercises it. Two rules make this true … Every catch in the closure rethrows EvalError.' The rule is stated as a property of the code, but nothing enforces it for a new handler: no lint selector covers CatchClause or TryStatement, no-unsafe-finally is off, and the scan has no such pattern (adr-claims.log A2).

swallow-probe.mjs puts a real string code generation on the round-3 S1 path (tokenize.ts describe() for U+00C0–U+1FFF; key from String.fromCharCode). W5 proves this path is exercised and refused under the flag. Three handler forms then pass ALL THREE layers (lint 0, scan 0, unit-formula-nocodegen 199 passed + 1 skipped, exit 0):
- W1: try { codegen } catch { }
- W2: try { codegen } finally { return; }
- W4: Promise.resolve().then(codegen).catch(() => undefined)
In production, with no flag, that code runs. The residual paragraph names only unexercised paths, plus a future catch converting to an 'internal' problem. It does not name a path that handles its own refusal.

Minor inaccuracies in the same section:
- 'There are four' catches: there are five clauses.
- 'the web formula builder would show its error boundary': the web defines no boundary. React Router's DefaultErrorComponent would show 'Unexpected Application Error!' with the error message and stack, in English only. This is unreachable in practice.
- 'following every static import and export … from': not string-named specifiers (X1, backed by ESLint).

CLOSURE CRITERIA (either suffices for me):
(a) Enforce the rethrow rule statically in the closure, in lint and mirrored in the scan. For example:
  - every CatchClause must rethrow EvalError first;
  - no-unsafe-finally on;
  - no Promise, `.then`, `.catch` or `.finally` in engine sources (the engine is synchronous).
  A self-handled codegen is then refused unless it uses an unexercised path, which is the stated residual.
(b) Narrow the §6 guarantee and add this residual honestly: code that handles its own refusal (catch, finally-return, .catch) is invisible to layer 3 even on an exercised path, the run-time analogue of the Q1–Q5 static residual. Also correct the three minor statements.

Reproduction (disposable clone only; files are restored):
- node docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG3/code-security/round-4/probes/swallow-probe.mjs $TMPDIR/review-p3 W1 W2 W4 W5
- Clone at 171a0b57 with deps installed offline.

findings.title: Inherited-approval badge does not wrap: it overflows the G1 card on the Gates list (EN and AR, every width) and makes the gate view scroll horizontally; in EN its '(does not approve this gate)' disclaimer is clipped
findings.reproduction: Disposable stack (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG3/domain/round-2/with-stack.sh), probe dg3-ui-overflow.mjs (PROBES=dg3-ui-overflow run-all.sh). Create a Modular transformation, record an inherited_approval of G1 with verified evidence, and have the synthetic Sponsor accept it. Sign in as dev.lead in EN and in AR at viewport widths 1024, 1366 and 1920. Open /transformations/{id}/gates and /transformations/{id}/gates/G1, then measure the [data-inherited-approval] box against its card and the document scrollWidth against the viewport. Cause: apps/web/src/styles/app.css .status-chip { white-space: nowrap } applies to the ~80-character label 'Inherited approval: accepted, counts for sequencing (does not approve this gate)'.
findings.expected: The badge (ADR-0021 §5, F-DG3-120 repair) stays inside its card or row and wraps, so its full text is visible, including the '(does not approve this gate)' / '(لا يعتمد هذه البوابة)' safeguard. The page never scrolls horizontally at common desktop widths in either direction.
findings.actual: Gates list: the EN badge is 518 px wide inside a ~335 px G1 card at 1024, 1366 and 1920 (box [310,828] vs card [297,632] at 1366). On screen it reads 'Inherited approval: accepted, counts for sequencing (' and is clipped, so the disclaimer is not visible. The AR badge (353 px) spills out of the card's left edge and overlaps the G2 card's approver line. Gate view: the badge spills out of its row and the document scrolls horizontally (EN scrollWidth 1604 at a 1366 viewport and 1170 at 1024; AR 1439 at 1366, where the badge starts at x=-73). So this is a presentation/readability defect of the new safeguard text, not an integrity failure. The jsdom unit test (inherited-approval.test.tsx) cannot see layout, so it passes.
